hooks.name: world_lifecycle
hooks.neoforge: ServerStartingEvent / ServerStartedEvent / ServerStoppedEvent (WorldOpenReady answers both Starting and Started; also told when a world fails to open or close)
hooks.signature: fn native_world_lifecycle( &mut self, context: &NativeLifecycleContext, phase: WorldPhase, error_text: &str, )
hooks.doc: The world's phases, read-only; `error_text` carries the engine's own open-failure text, empty otherwise. Server-side. A server loop or final save failure fires `WorldCloseFailed` with the error text.

hooks.name: server_about_to_start
hooks.signature: fn native_server_about_to_start(&mut self, dedicated: bool)
hooks.doc: The server is about to open its worlds: nothing of the world is loaded yet (NeoForge's `ServerAboutToStartEvent`, "called before the server begins loading anything"). Vanilla's `MinecraftServer.loadLevel` start. Server-side: the single player server thread once Play is pressed, a dedicated server once its settings are read. Each is followed by `native_world_lifecycle`'s `WorldOpenReady` or `WorldOpenFailed`. `dedicated` tells a dedicated server from the single player one. API 44.

hooks.name: server_stopping
hooks.signature: fn native_server_stopping(&mut self, dedicated: bool)
hooks.doc: The server begins an orderly stop (NeoForge's `ServerStoppingEvent`): the start of vanilla's `MinecraftServer.stopServer`, with the worlds still loaded and the players still connected and not yet saved, so a mod can save its own data or tell them. `native_world_lifecycle`'s `WorldCloseFinal` follows once the worlds are saved. A server whose loop fails stops without this (`WorldCloseFailed` reports it). API 44.

hooks.name: server_tick
hooks.signature: fn native_server_tick( &mut self, context: &NativeLifecycleContext, phase: ServerTickPhase, )
hooks.doc: The authoritative server tick's phases: `ServerTickStart` before any level is ticked (NeoForge's `ServerTickEvent.Pre`), `ServerTickEnd` after the last (`.Post`). Read blocks with `native_server_block`, by dimension: which level `self.world` holds here is not defined. A paused pass fires nothing; a frozen world carries `world_running` false except during a requested step.

hooks.name: level_tick_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_level_tick_pre(&mut self, dimension: &str)
hooks.doc: Before an authoritative server level's tick pass. `dimension` is its ID.

hooks.name: level_tick_post
hooks.signature: fn native_level_tick_post(&mut self, dimension: &str)
hooks.doc: After a successful authoritative server level tick pass.

hooks.name: block_changed
hooks.signature: fn native_block_changed( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, old: BlockStateId, new: BlockStateId, )
hooks.doc: An authoritative server committed a changed state through `Level.setBlock`. The world contains `new`; block side effects and neighbour updates follow.

hooks.name: neighbor_changed
hooks.signature: fn native_neighbor_changed( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, changed: BlockId, moved: bool, )
hooks.doc: An authoritative server is about to deliver `neighborChanged`. State and block IDs are valid in this level's registries for this call.

hooks.name: random_tick
hooks.signature: fn native_random_tick( &mut self, ticks: &mut Ticks, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, handled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: An authoritative server's `ServerLevel.tickChunk` is about to random-tick the block `state` at `pos` (`BlockState.randomTick`): only blocks that tick randomly, a mod's as its vanilla template block does. Bone meal's random ticks (`StemBlock.performBonemeal`) don't fire it. Change the block with `native_set_block_property` and set `handled` to skip the block's own random tick (a mod crop growing its own way); a block changed without `handled` takes its own random tick as it is now, if it still ticks randomly. Lava's fluid random tick runs either way.

hooks.name: tick_block
hooks.signature: fn native_tick_block( &mut self, ticks: &mut Ticks, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, handled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: An authoritative server's `ServerLevel.tickBlock` is about to run a due scheduled tick of the block `state` at `pos` (`BlockState.tick`): the block is still the one the tick was scheduled for. Change the block with `native_set_block_property` and set `handled` to skip the block's own tick; a block changed without `handled` takes its own tick as it is now, if it is still the tick's block.

hooks.name: update_shape
hooks.signature: fn native_update_shape( &self, ticks: &mut Ticks, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, direction: Direction, neighbour_pos: BlockPos, neighbour: BlockStateId, new: &mut Option<BlockStateId>, )
hooks.doc: An authoritative server is about to compute the state the block `state` at `pos` takes now that its neighbour in `direction` is `neighbour` (`BlockBehaviour.updateShape`). `state` may not be in the world yet (a piston landing it): decide from `state`, not from the block at `pos`. Answer only for your own blocks: put the new state in `new` (`state` keeps the block as it is; air breaks it, with its drops, on a neighbour update) and the block's own `updateShape` doesn't run, nor the ticks it would schedule. The level is read-only, as vanilla's `LevelReader`; ticks go through `native_schedule_block_tick` and `native_schedule_fluid_tick` with `ticks` (`ScheduledTickAccess`). It runs often, at least six times per `setBlock` that updates shapes (more for redstone wire's diagonals and knock-on updates): keep it short.

hooks.name: hud
hooks.signature: fn native_hud(&mut self, batch: &mut HudBatch, corners: &mut Corners)
hooks.doc: The HUD (not drawn under F1), after the minimap: place a box with `corners.place` (boxes stack away from their edge) and draw it with `native_fill` and `native_text`. Skip a corner `native_corner_shown` says is taken.

hooks.name: key
hooks.signature: fn native_key(&mut self, key: &str, pressed: bool)
hooks.doc: A key or mouse button went down or up, by its vanilla name (`key.keyboard.z`, `key.mouse.left`): keys on any screen (check `native_playing`), mouse buttons while playing. Repeats are left out.

hooks.name: wheel
hooks.signature: fn native_wheel(&mut self, steps: f32, claimed: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: Wheel steps while playing: set `claimed` to keep them from the hotbar.

hooks.name: command
hooks.signature: fn native_command(&mut self, command: &str, ran: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: A command typed or clicked in chat, without its slash, before the server and Horizon's commands see it: set `ran` when the mod ran it.

hooks.name: commands
hooks.signature: fn native_commands(&mut self, commands: &mut Vec<&'static str>)
hooks.doc: The commands `native_command` runs, by name and without their slash: push the ones that are yours. Asked when a connection starts and again when the server sends its own tree, so the chat box colours, completes and lists them as the game's own; a name the game already has keeps that command's behaviour. API 35.

hooks.name: zoom
hooks.signature: fn native_zoom(&self, zoom: &mut Option<NativeZoom>)
hooks.doc: The zoom a native mod asks for, applied while playing (the spyglass's own view wins): set `zoom` when it is none yet.

hooks.name: minimap
