hooks.name: settings
hooks.signature: fn native_settings(&mut self, mod_id: &str, buttons: &mut Vec<String>)
hooks.doc: The buttons of mod `mod_id`'s settings page, under its keys: push their labels when it is yours. Asked again each time the page opens and after each click.

hooks.name: settings_click
hooks.signature: fn native_settings_click(&mut self, mod_id: &str, button: usize)
hooks.doc: Button `button` of mod `mod_id`'s settings page was clicked.

hooks.name: panel_event
hooks.signature: fn native_panel_event(&mut self, mod_id: &str, event: &NativePanelEvent)
hooks.doc: The player did `event` on mod `mod_id`'s panel (`native_panel_items`): act on it when it is yours. API 2.

hooks.name: block_entity
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity( &mut self, block: &str, entity: &mut Option<(String, Compound)>, )
hooks.doc: Block `block` (`mymod:machine`) gets a block entity (`EntityBlock.newBlockEntity`): set `entity` to its id and saved compound when the block is yours and `entity` is none yet. It works on any template: the engine removes the block entity when its block is broken or replaced, no piston moves it, and a mod that draws it (`native_block_entity_submit`) is asked for it. API 15; before 129 the block's template had to have a block entity of its own (a chest, a furnace...), or the block got none.

hooks.name: block_entity_ticks
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity_ticks(&self, block: &str, ticks: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: Whether block `block`'s block entity ticks (`EntityBlock.getTicker`): set `ticks` when it is yours. Asked for each of the block's states when a world opens. API 15. Set `ticks` to true to make it tick, and never clear a value an earlier mod or mixin set.

hooks.name: block_entity_tick
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity_tick(&mut self, pos: [i32; 3], entity: &mut ModBlockEntity)
hooks.doc: A server tick of the block entity at `pos`, in vanilla's order among the others (`Level.tickBlockEntities`), when its `id` is yours: read and change its saved compound `nbt`, its item slots `items` (keep their count: as many as its container has, none without one) and the data slots its menu shows (`data`). It is out of the world during the call (the block entity at `pos` reads as a `Mod` with an empty id, and a save leaves it out); if the call removes or replaces it, `entity` is dropped. Clients, the window's own in single player included, get what `native_block_entity_update_tag` gives when its chunk is sent or its block changes. API 17.

hooks.name: block_entity_update_tag
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity_update_tag( pos: [i32; 3], entity: &ModBlockEntity, tag: &mut Option<Compound>, )
hooks.doc: What clients get of the block entity at `pos` when its `id` is yours (`BlockEntity.getUpdateTag`): set `tag` to it, read from `entity` alone. Asked on the server whenever a chunk holding it is sent and whenever its block changes, on the server thread or, for a saved chunk sent past the view distance (`lan::far`), another one; a client's copy of the block entity (made by `native_block_entity` there) merges it into its `nbt`. An owner can merge `entity.take_client_update_fields()` into this tag for one-shot fields that are neither saved nor cloned. The tag is constructed once before a block change is broadcast to its viewers. Leave it unset to send nothing. API 45.

hooks.name: block_entity_container
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity_container( &self, block: &str, container: &mut Option<ModContainer>, )
hooks.doc: Block `block`'s block entity has item slots (a `WorldlyContainer`): set `container` when the block is yours. Asked once for each mod block when the ticking table is built; at most 256 slots, and slot numbers past the count are left out. Its `menu`, one of `containers::MOD_MENUS` or a content mod's menu type (`data/<id>/horizon/menu/`, API 85) with as many slots, opens when the block is used (its template must open a menu, as a chest or a furnace does); another is left out. A mod menu type shows on Horizon clients through the mod's `native_screen` only. API 17.

hooks.name: screen
hooks.signature: fn native_screen(&self, block: &str, screen: &mut Option<NativeScreen>)
hooks.doc: A menu opens on this client for block `block`, a mod's: set `screen` when the block is yours, to lay its screen out (`native_screen_draw` draws it). The server asks it too: a slot it hides is not in the menu there either, so shift-clicks never fill it. API 19.

hooks.name: screen_draw
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_draw( &self, block: &str, data: &[i32], batch: &mut HudBatch, origin: [f32; 2], )
hooks.doc: Draw block `block`'s screen at `origin` (its top left, GUI pixels), over a plain panel with its slots' frames and under the items and labels, from the menu's data slots `data` (the block entity's `data` on the server): data slots are 16-bit on the wire as in vanilla (a bigger value wraps), and `data` is empty until the server's first values arrive, so read it with `get`. Draw with `native_sprite`, `native_fill` and `native_text`. API 19.

hooks.name: screen_click
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_click( &self, block: &str, data: &[i32], at: [f32; 2], right: bool, button: &mut Option<i32>, )
hooks.doc: A left or right (`right`) press at `at` (GUI pixels from the screen's top left, so outside it too) on block `block`'s screen, a mod's, over no slot: set `button` to a menu button id when it is on one of yours. Horizon sends it to the server (`ContainerButtonClick`, `native_menu_button` there) and the press goes no further. API 20.

hooks.name: screen_tooltip
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_tooltip( &self, block: &str, data: &[i32], at: [f32; 2], lines: &mut Vec<String>, )
hooks.doc: The tooltip at `at` (as in `native_screen_click`) on block `block`'s screen, a mod's, over no item: push its lines when it is over something of yours. Legacy colour codes (§) work. API 20.

hooks.name: menu_button
hooks.signature: fn native_menu_button( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], entity: &mut ModBlockEntity, id: i32, )
hooks.doc: A player pressed menu button `id` on the menu of the mod block entity at `pos` (`AbstractContainerMenu.clickMenuButton`), on the server: change `entity` when its id is yours. It is out of the world during the call, as in `native_block_entity_tick`. API 20.

hooks.name: register_commands
hooks.signature: fn native_register_commands(&mut self, commands: &mut Vec<NativeCommand>)
hooks.doc: The commands native mods add to the server's command tree: push yours. Asked once when a world opens to players (a dedicated server, a LAN host, single player's server thread); every player's chat box then completes them as vanilla's, within their level. A name vanilla has is left out. Asked again after a mod calls `native_refresh_commands`. API 8.

hooks.name: perform_command
hooks.signature: fn native_perform_command( &mut self, player: &NativeServerPlayer, command: &str, ran: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player's command on the server (`Commands.performCommand`), without its slash, for a command a mod registered and the player's level allows: set `ran` when it is yours. The player's state is swapped in for the call, so `native_player` and the other helpers read that player; `native_feedback` answers them. A single player's owner console (`horizon-ctl command`) reaches it too, as the owner at level 4. API 8.

hooks.name: menu_clicked
hooks.signature: fn native_menu_clicked( &mut self, uuid: u128, window: i32, slot: i32, button: i32, mode: i32, )
hooks.doc: A click in a menu a mod opened (`native_open_menu`), which moved nothing: the menu's `slot` (its own first, then the player's inventory, `native_menu_inventory_slot`; -999 outside), the `button` and the click's `mode` (`ClickType`'s id) of the player `uuid`. No player's state is swapped in: the menu helpers take the player's UUID. API 10.

hooks.name: menu_closed
hooks.signature: fn native_menu_closed(&mut self, uuid: u128, window: i32)
hooks.doc: A menu a mod opened closed: the player closed it, the server or a mod opened another, or the player left. API 10.

hooks.name: tooltip
hooks.signature: fn native_tooltip(&self, stack: &ItemStack, lines: &mut Vec<(Text, u32)>)
hooks.doc: An item's tooltip, wherever the game shows one (slots, the creative tabs, the recipe book, chat's hover): the stack, with its components (`stack.data()`: a shulker box's contents...), and its lines, the name first, each with a colour as `rgba` packs it (`u32::MAX` keeps the text's own). Add, change or take out lines; `Text::legacy` reads `§` codes. Asked each frame the tooltip shows, never for one the stack hides. API 12.

hooks.name: use_item_on
hooks.signature: fn native_use_item_on( &mut self, stack: &ItemStack, pos: [i32; 3], face: [i32; 3], claimed: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player uses `stack` (right click) with `self.hand` on the block at `pos`, `face` the face clicked (`[0, 1, 0]` is the top), once the block itself let the click through (a chest still opens): where `ItemStack.useOn` starts. Set `claimed` to take the use: the hand swings and neither the item's `useOn` nor its `use` runs. Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one); an item on cooldown is never used. API 13.

hooks.name: use_item
hooks.signature: fn native_use_item(&mut self, stack: &ItemStack, claimed: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: A player uses `stack` (right click) with `self.hand`: in the air, or on a block once `native_use_item_on` let it through, where `Item.use` starts. Each click reaches it once. Set `claimed` to take the use: the hand swings and the item's own use doesn't run. Server-side, for every player of the world; an item on cooldown is never used. API 13.

hooks.name: destroy_block
hooks.signature: fn native_destroy_block( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], state: BlockStateId, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player breaks the block `state` at `pos`, once the game allowed it (the held item can break blocks, the debug stick didn't take the click): where `ServerPlayerGameMode.destroyBlock` starts. Set `canceled` to keep the block: nothing is destroyed or dropped, and a guest sees it back. Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one). API 14.

hooks.name: place_block
hooks.neoforge: BlockEvent.EntityPlaceEvent (hears only: a mod stops a placement by claiming use_item_on)
hooks.signature: fn native_place_block( &mut self, stack: &ItemStack, pos: [i32; 3], state: BlockStateId, )
hooks.doc: A player placed `stack` as the block `state` at `pos`: where `BlockItem.place` set it, before the stack shrinks. It only hears; a mod stops a placement by claiming `native_use_item_on`, which runs before it. Server-side, for every player of the world. API 14.

hooks.name: right_click_block
hooks.signature: fn native_right_click_block( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], face: [i32; 3], canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player right clicks the block at `pos` with `self.hand`, `face` the face clicked: where `ServerPlayerGameMode.useItemOn` starts, before the block's own use (a chest, a door, a lever) and before `native_use_item_on`. Set `canceled` to stop the click: neither the block nor the item acts, the hand doesn't swing, and a guest sees the block as it is. Server-side, for every player of the world (`native_acting_player` says who), once per hand. API 21.

hooks.name: block_spread
hooks.signature: fn native_block_spread( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, kind: &str, from: BlockPos, to: BlockPos, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: On an authoritative server, a fluid flows or fire spreads from `from` into `to` (`kind` is `fluid` or `fire`): `FlowingFluid.spreadTo`, and `FireBlock.tick` setting fire to `to` or burning it (`checkBurnOut`). Set `canceled` to leave the block at `to` as it is. Fluids ask on every flow: answer fast. API 22.

hooks.name: piston_move
hooks.signature: fn native_piston_move( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, piston: BlockPos, direction: [i32; 3], push: &[BlockPos], destroy: &[BlockPos], canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: On an authoritative server, the piston at `piston` is about to push the blocks at `push` one step `direction` (`[0, 1, 0]` is up; pulling when it retracts) and destroy those at `destroy`: `PistonBaseBlock.moveBlocks`, once its structure resolved. Set `canceled` and nothing moves, as when the structure can't; a sticky piston then retracts without its block, and clients are sent the blocks rather than the retraction to replay. API 22.

hooks.name: explosion_detonate
hooks.neoforge: ExplosionEvent.Detonate (blocks only: entities are hurt as before)
hooks.signature: fn native_explosion_detonate( &mut self, dimension: &str, center: [f64; 3], source: Option<(u32, &str)>, blocks: &mut Vec<[i32; 3]>, )
hooks.doc: An explosion at `center` in `dimension` (`minecraft:overworld`) is about to break `blocks`: `ServerExplosion.explode` with its `toBlow`, before any block is hit. Take out the positions to spare; they keep their block and get no fire. Entities are hurt as before. Server-side. `source` is the entity that exploded (TNT, a minecart of TNT, a creeper, a large fireball, an end crystal) with its kind, when the engine knows it; `None` for the other blasts. API 22.

hooks.name: fill_bucket
hooks.signature: fn native_fill_bucket( &mut self, stack: &ItemStack, pos: [i32; 3], canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player fills (`stack` an empty bucket) or empties a bucket at `pos`: `BucketItem.use`, where it asks `Level.mayInteract`. Set `canceled` and the bucket does nothing. Server-side, for every player of the world (`native_acting_player` says who). API 22.

hooks.name: attack_entity
hooks.signature: fn native_attack_entity( &mut self, entity: i32, kind: &str, pos: [f64; 3], canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player attacks the entity `entity` (`Entity.getId`) of type `kind` (`minecraft:item_frame`, `minecraft:cow`, `minecraft:player`) standing at `pos`: `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleInteract`'s attack, once in reach, where `Player.attack` starts. Set `canceled` and the blow does nothing (no damage, no knockback, the frame keeps its item). Server-side, for every player of the world (`native_acting_player` says who). API 22.

hooks.name: net_from_client
hooks.signature: fn native_net_from_client(&mut self, player: u128, channel: &str, data: &[u8])
hooks.doc: A message from `player`'s client on `channel` (`mod_id:name`), within the caps (`native_net.rs`): check `channel`, and treat `data` as the player's own bytes, checked by nothing. Runs in the tick after it arrives, with no player's state swapped in. Server-side. API 40.

hooks.name: net_from_server
hooks.signature: fn native_net_from_server(&mut self, channel: &str, data: &[u8])
hooks.doc: A message from the server on `channel` (`mod_id:name`), whose `data` is the sender's own bytes. The window's game only. API 40.

hooks.name: player_died
hooks.signature: fn native_player_died(&mut self, player: u128, cause: Option<&str>)
hooks.doc: `player` died: where `ServerPlayer.die` starts, with the death message's key when the game knows it (`death.attack.lava`; none for a message it builds from the combat). It only hears. Server-side, for every player of the world, whether death messages are shown or not. API 40.

hooks.name: mob_spawned
hooks.signature: fn native_mob_spawned( &mut self, dimension: &str, kind: &str, pos: [f64; 3], natural: bool, )
hooks.doc: A new mob of `kind` joined `dimension` at `pos`: `natural` when the world's spawning made it, false when something else did (a breed, a raid, a spawner, a conversion, `/summon`, and the second mob of a jockey the world spawned). One call a mob: a `/summon` with passengers tells each. Not told of a mob loaded with its chunk, leaving a hive or changing level. It only hears; the mob is already among the game's mobs. Server-side. API 40.

hooks.name: mob_killed
hooks.signature: fn native_mob_killed(&mut self, player: u128, entity: u32, kind: &str)
hooks.doc: `player`'s melee blow killed the mob `entity` of `kind` (other deaths aren't told yet). It only hears, after the blow landed. Server-side. API 40.

hooks.name: item_dropped
hooks.neoforge: ItemTossEvent (only hears: a toss can't be canceled)
hooks.signature: fn native_item_dropped(&mut self, player: u128, item: &str, count: u32)
hooks.doc: `player` threw `count` of `item` (`Player.drop`: the drop key, a menu's throw...), not what scatters when they die. It only hears. Server-side. API 40.

hooks.name: item_picked_up
hooks.neoforge: ItemEntityPickupEvent.Pre (canceled is setCanPickup(TriState.FALSE); no forced pickup)
hooks.signature: fn native_item_picked_up( &mut self, player: u128, item: &str, count: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: `player` is about to take `count` of `item` from the ground (`ItemEntity.playerTouch`). Set `canceled` to leave it there: the stack isn't offered again for 10 ticks. Server-side. API 40.

hooks.name: hurt_enemy
hooks.signature: fn native_hurt_enemy(&mut self, stack: &ItemStack, entity: u32, kind: &str)
hooks.doc: A player's hit landed on the mob `entity` of type `kind` (`minecraft:zombie`), holding `stack`: where `Item.hurtEnemy` is called, before the post-attack enchantments and the weapon's wear. It only hears. Another player as the target isn't told yet. Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one). API 39.

hooks.name: inventory_tick
hooks.signature: fn native_inventory_tick(&mut self, slot: i32, selected: bool)
hooks.doc: A server tick of the stack a player carries in `slot`: where `Inventory.tick` calls `Item.inventoryTick`, for every stack, each tick, `/tick freeze` included (it stops the world, not the player). `slot` is as `Inventory` saves it (0 to 35; the armour 100 feet to 103 head; -106 the off hand), and `selected` says it is the held slot. `native_carried_stack` reads and changes the stack, which stays in its slot, so the item helpers see it: a count of 0 empties the slot, and the player's client gets the change. This runs often, so check the item first. Server-side, for every living player of the world (the helpers read the acting one). API 39.

hooks.name: on_equip
hooks.signature: fn native_on_equip(&mut self, slot: &str, new: Option<&ItemStack>)
hooks.doc: A player's equipment slot `slot` (`head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet`, `offhand`, and `mainhand` on a swap of the hands or `/item`) took a different item, `new` (none when it was emptied): `LivingEntity.onEquipItem`, before the equip sound. It only hears. Never for a spectator. Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one). API 39.

hooks.name: block_signal
hooks.signature: fn native_block_signal( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, face: Direction, direct: bool, signal: &mut i32, )
hooks.doc: The redstone signal the block `state` at `pos` gives on its `face`, the side that touches the block reading it: `BlockState.getDirectSignal` when `direct` (what passes through a block it touches, as a lever's does), else `getSignal`. `signal` holds vanilla's answer: change it when the block is yours (0 to 15; anything else is clamped). Asked very often, from inside the level's update, so answer from your own state: check the block first, and don't read or change the world here. When the answer changes, and once the block is placed, call `native_update_signal_neighbors`. Authoritative servers only. API 38.

hooks.name: is_signal_source
hooks.signature: fn native_is_signal_source(&self, state: BlockStateId, source: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: `BlockState.isSignalSource`: set `source` for a block of yours that gives a signal, so redstone wire beside it connects to it. Authoritative servers only. API 38.

hooks.name: health_hud
hooks.signature: fn native_health_hud( &mut self, inputs: &horizon_client::hud_layout::HealthInputs, wi: i32, hi: i32, draws: &mut Option<Vec<horizon_client::hud_layout::GuiDraw>>, )
hooks.doc: The player-health HUD rows, once a frame the HUD draws them (`HealthHud::layout`, not under F1): `inputs` carries the health, food, air and vehicle state the layout reads, `wi`/`hi` the screen's GUI size. A mod that sets `draws` replaces every row — armour, hearts, food and air are the answer's to give; `bubble_pop_sound` too. Nothing set draws Horizon's own.

hooks.name: interact_entity
hooks.signature: fn native_interact_entity( &mut self, entity: i32, kind: &str, stack: Option<&ItemStack>, claimed: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player right-clicks the entity `entity` (`Entity.getId`) of type `kind` (`minecraft:cow`) with `self.hand`, holding `stack` (none in an empty hand): where `Player.interactOn` starts, before the entity's own `interact` and the item's `interactLivingEntity`. Set `claimed` to take the click: the hand swings and neither runs. Asked once per hand, as vanilla tries the main hand then the off hand. Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one). API 29.

hooks.name: left_click_block
hooks.signature: fn native_left_click_block( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], face: [i32; 3], state: BlockStateId, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player left-clicks the block `state` at `pos`, `face` the face hit (`[0, 1, 0]` is the top): where `ServerPlayerGameMode.handleBlockBreakAction` takes a dig's start, after its reach, spawn protection and world border checks, before `Block.attack` (a note block plays) or a creative break. Set `canceled` to ignore the click: the block isn't attacked, dug or broken on the server, and the player's client gets it back (its own predicted crack still shows to the clicking player). Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one). API 30.

hooks.name: player_tick
hooks.signature: fn native_player_tick(&mut self)
hooks.doc: A living player's server tick ends (`ServerPlayer.tick`): once a tick for every player in the world, after their digging, item use, cooldowns, statistics and advancements. The helpers read that player. Players still tick under `/tick freeze`; a dead player doesn't, nor does one killed earlier in the same tick. API 31.

hooks.name: entity_join_level
hooks.signature: fn native_entity_join_level( &mut self, dimension: &str, entity: u32, kind: &str, pos: [f64; 3], loaded_from_disk: bool, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: An entity joins the server level `dimension` (NeoForge's `EntityJoinLevelEvent`): vanilla's `PersistentEntitySectionManager.addEntity`. `loaded_from_disk` is true for an entity coming back with its chunk, false for one added fresh (`addFreshEntity`: a drop, an orb, `/summon`, an arrival through a portal). `entity` is its ID and `kind` its type (`minecraft:item`). It is already in the level's lists, so helpers that take an entity ID find it. Set `canceled` to keep it out: it is taken back out as if never added, and a `/summon` of it fails. Tells every kind in the game's entity lists (items, orbs, mobs, boats, minecarts, armor stands, primed TNT, falling blocks, projectiles, rockets, tridents, end crystals, the dragon, cushions, paintings, item frames), and the entities Horizon keeps without simulating (block, item and text displays, markers, interactions), once each, in the order they were created; check `kind`. A drop, an orb, a mob, a `/summon` and a chunk's entities are told at once, any other spawn between the tick's phases (it is checked after the blocks, the vehicles, the projectiles, the items and the mobs, and at the tick's end). A mod that cancels one of the others sees it removed before it ticks again. Server-side.

hooks.name: living_incoming_damage
hooks.signature: fn native_living_incoming_damage( entity: i32, kind: &str, damage_type: &str, causing: i32, direct: i32, amount: &mut f32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: `LivingEntity.hurtServer`, past its guards (invulnerable, dead, fire with fire resistance), is about to hurt entity `entity` of type `kind` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:player`) by `amount` of `damage_type` (`minecraft:fall`), from the source's `causing` entity (`DamageSource.getEntity`: the shooter of an arrow) and `direct` one (`getDirectEntity`: the arrow), 0 for none or not known yet (docs/native-mods.md, API 50). Change `amount`, or set `canceled`, and nothing of `hurtServer` itself happens (no damage, hurt sound, knockback, invulnerable time, statistics or criteria); the caller acts as on a refused hit, except that a canceled hit on the ender dragon still counts as landed (`EnderDragon.hurt` returns true whatever `reallyHurt` did: the arrow is spent, the melee effects run). It runs on the thread that ticks the world (the server thread): state shared with render thread hooks needs synchronising. No `self`: the game is in the middle of the hit. API 50.

hooks.name: menu_button_v2
hooks.signature: fn native_menu_button_v2( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], entity: &mut ModBlockEntity, id: i32, carried: &mut Option<ItemStack>, )
hooks.doc: `AbstractContainerMenu.clickMenuButton(Player, int)`'s other half: the acting player's cursor stack, `getCarried()`/`setCarried()`, which `native_menu_button` cannot reach. Fires right after it, same moment, same `pos`/`entity`/`id`; change `carried` when its id is yours. On the server. API 51.

hooks.name: entity_leave_level
hooks.signature: fn native_entity_leave_level(&mut self, dimension: &str, entity: u32, kind: &str)
hooks.doc: An entity leaves the server level `dimension` (NeoForge's `EntityLeaveLevelEvent`): vanilla's `onTrackingEnd`, when it is removed for any reason (picked up, merged, despawned, burnt, blown up, killed, taken by a hopper or a mob, gone through a portal) or its chunk unloads, a level closing with nobody in it included. Not for the entities still loaded when the server stops, as in vanilla. `entity` is its ID and `kind` its type (`minecraft:item`); it is no longer in the level's lists. It only hears. 53 told item entities, experience orbs and mobs; it now tells every kind `native_entity_join_level` does (`kind` is the type), each once, when the game next notices it gone (the tick or action that removed it). Check `kind`. Server-side.

hooks.name: block_entity_fluids
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity_fluids( &self, block: &str, fluids: &mut Option<ModFluidTanks>, )
hooks.doc: Block `block`'s block entity has fluid tanks: set `fluids` when the block is yours, in the container's shape — each tank's capacity in millibuckets, the tanks each face reaches, and the tanks a fill may reach and a drain may take. Asked once for each mod block when the ticking table is built; at most 16 tanks, capacities clamped to 1..=1 000 000, and tank numbers past the count are left out. The tanks' contents are kept in the entity's saved compound, under `fluids`, and the fluid helpers below read and write them. API 54.

hooks.name: should_apply_effect_tick_this_tick
hooks.signature: fn native_should_apply_effect_tick_this_tick( &self, effect: &str, tick_count: i32, amplifier: i32, apply: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: `MobEffect.shouldApplyEffectTickThisTick` for a content mod's effect `effect` (`ruby:bleeding`), each tick a player or a mob has it, in `MobEffectInstance.tickServer` before it counts down: `tick_count` is the ticks left (the entity's tick count when infinite). Set `apply` and `native_apply_effect_tick` follows. Server-side. API 56.

hooks.name: apply_effect_tick
hooks.signature: fn native_apply_effect_tick( &self, effect: &str, dimension: &str, entity: Option<i32>, amplifier: i32, keep: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: `MobEffect.applyEffectTick`: the content mod's effect `effect` acts on `entity` in `dimension` (`minecraft:overworld`). Clear `keep` and the effect ends now, before it counts down. `entity` is a mob's `Entity.getId`, None for a player (`native_acting_player` says who). It runs inside the entity's tick: a mob's world borrows the game there, so the game is read-only, and it does not hold the ticking mobs, nor the player's effects. Server-side. API 56.

hooks.name: on_effect_added
hooks.signature: fn native_on_effect_added( &mut self, effect: &str, entity: Option<i32>, amplifier: i32, )
hooks.doc: `MobEffect.onEffectAdded`: `LivingEntity.addEffect` gave `entity` (as in `native_apply_effect_tick`) the content mod's effect `effect`, which it didn't have. Server-side. API 56.

hooks.name: mob_effect_added
hooks.signature: fn native_mob_effect_added( &mut self, effect: &str, entity: Option<i32>, amplifier: i32, )
hooks.doc: NeoForge's `MobEffectEvent.Added`, vanilla's `MobEffect.onEffectStarted`: every `LivingEntity.addEffect` of the content mod's effect `effect`, new or not, changed or not, after `native_on_effect_added`. Server-side. API 56.

hooks.name: chunk_load
hooks.signature: fn native_chunk_load(&mut self, dimension: &str, chunk: [i32; 2], new: bool)
hooks.doc: Chunk `chunk` (`[x, z]`, in chunks) of `dimension` came into the world (NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Load`): `new` when it was just generated, false when read from the save. A flat world's chunk that leaves before it's first lit isn't saved, so it's generated, and new, again; one generated as the players left is new when it next comes, unless the server restarts first, or the level closes for being empty, which drops its memory of what never saved. Its blocks and block entities are there, but its saved entities join afterwards and its light may not be ready: change the world from a later tick. The chunks around the spawn come before `WorldOpenReady`. Not told of a chunk a client receives. Server-side. API 57.

hooks.name: chunk_unload
hooks.signature: fn native_chunk_unload(&mut self, dimension: &str, chunk: [i32; 2])
hooks.doc: Chunk `chunk` of `dimension` left the world (NeoForge's `ChunkEvent.Unload`), with a level that closes for being empty too. Don't read its blocks. Its block entities are still there for this call, so `native_with_mod_block_entity` can change one and it's saved with the chunk. Not told when the world closes, which `native_world_lifecycle` tells. Server-side. API 57.

hooks.name: player_logged_in
hooks.signature: fn native_player_logged_in(&mut self, player: u128, name: &str)
hooks.doc: `player` (`name`) joined the game (NeoForge's `PlayerLoggedInEvent`): placed in the world and listed in `native_server_players`, so `native_net_send_to_player` reaches them. Once a join, with no player's state swapped in. Server-side. API 57.

hooks.name: player_logged_out
hooks.signature: fn native_player_logged_out(&mut self, player: u128, name: &str)
hooks.doc: `player` (`name`) left the game (NeoForge's `PlayerLoggedOutEvent`), by any path: a lost connection, a kick, the server stopping or failing. Once for each player `native_player_logged_in` told of. They've already left `native_server_players`, except when the server stops, which tells before it saves, with them still listed and able to get a last message. Server-side. API 57.

hooks.name: world_drawn
hooks.neoforge: RenderLevelStageEvent (the drawn world's colour, depth and matrices, once the whole level is drawn, before the hand)

hooks.name: item_bar
hooks.signature: fn native_item_bar(&self, stack: &ItemStack, bar: &mut Option<(i32, u32)>)
hooks.doc: The small bar `GuiGraphicsExtractor.itemDecorations` draws under an item, wherever the game shows one: `bar` arrives holding vanilla's value (the damage bar, or a bundle's fullness already applied) and may be replaced (width `0..=13`, colour `rgb`) or set to `None` to hide it. Asked each frame a stack is drawn. Client-side. 60.

hooks.name: has_analog_output
hooks.signature: fn native_has_analog_output(&self, state: BlockStateId, output: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: `BlockState.hasAnalogOutputSignal`: set `output` for a block of yours that comparators read (how full or far along it is, as a composter's level), so they ask `native_analog_output`. Asked from inside the level's update: answer from `state` alone. Authoritative servers only. API 64.

hooks.name: analog_output
hooks.signature: fn native_analog_output( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, face: Direction, output: &mut i32, )
hooks.doc: `BlockState.getAnalogOutputSignal`: the signal a comparator reads from the block `state` at `pos`, `face` the side that touches the comparator (or the conductor in front of it). `output` holds vanilla's answer: change it when the block is yours (0 to 15; anything else is clamped). Asked only for blocks `native_has_analog_output` answered for, from inside the level's update: don't change the world here. When the answer changes without the block's state changing, call `native_update_output_neighbors`; a change of state through `native_set_block` or `native_set_block_property` (neighbour updates on) tells the comparators itself, as vanilla's `Level.setBlock` does. Authoritative servers only. API 64.

hooks.name: component_types
hooks.signature: fn native_component_types(types: &mut Vec<String>)
hooks.doc: Register namespaced NBT component types before content loads.

hooks.name: dispense_item
hooks.signature: fn native_dispense_item( &mut self, dimension: &str, pos: [i32; 3], facing: Direction, stack: &ItemStack, answer: &mut Option<NativeDispensed>, )
hooks.doc: `DispenserBlock.getDispenseMethod`: choose a behaviour for any item, including vanilla items, on the authoritative server (not droppers). Leave answer None for vanilla. Otherwise answer `(remainder, event)`: a remainder of None empties the slot, `Some(stack)` replaces it (the hook owns consumption: no extra item is removed afterwards). `event` is the level event the dispenser plays with its smoke: 1000 the click, 1001 the fail sound (`OptionalDispenseItemBehavior` without success), or 0 for nothing at all (`DispenseItemBehavior.NOOP`). To drop one normally, answer `(native_dispense_default(..), 1000)`. API 67.

hooks.name: tooltip_component
hooks.neoforge: RenderTooltipEvent.GatherComponents (one image component after the text, drawn by tooltip_component_draw)
hooks.signature: fn native_tooltip_component(&self, stack: &ItemStack, size: &mut Option<[f32; 2]>)
hooks.doc: Client-side image component for this stack's tooltip. Answer its width/height in GUI pixels; finite positive dimensions reserve space after text and any vanilla bundle component. None keeps the vanilla tooltip unchanged.

hooks.name: tooltip_component_draw
hooks.signature: fn native_tooltip_component_draw( &self, stack: &ItemStack, batch: &mut HudBatch, origin: [f32; 2], size: [f32; 2], )
hooks.doc: Render the measured component at origin, inside the tooltip background. Stack is the component's data. Use native_sprite/native_fill/native_text; size is the measurement returned by native_tooltip_component this frame.

hooks.name: can_survive
hooks.signature: fn native_can_survive( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, survives: &mut Option<bool>, )
hooks.doc: On an authoritative server, `BlockState.canSurvive` for `state` at `pos` (`BlockBehaviour.canSurvive`), before the block answers it: as it is placed (`BlockItem.canPlace`), from a shape update of a block whose template checks it (a plant, a torch, a sign: false breaks the block with its drops), and wherever else vanilla asks. `state` may not be in the world yet, so decide from `state`. Answer only for your own blocks: `Some(false)` refuses the spot, `Some(true)` allows it, and the block's own rule doesn't run. The level is read-only. Asked on every shape update of such a block: keep it short. API 70.

hooks.name: may_place_on
hooks.signature: fn native_may_place_on( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, state: BlockStateId, ground: BlockStateId, ground_pos: BlockPos, may: &mut Option<bool>, )
hooks.doc: On an authoritative server, `VegetationBlock.mayPlaceOn` for the plant `state` on `ground` at `ground_pos`, before the plant answers it: the blocks a mod plant (one whose template is a vanilla plant, such as a crop) can stand on. Its template's `canSurvive` asks it, so the plant is refused there and pops off when its ground changes to one it can't stand on. Answer only for your own blocks. The level is read-only. API 70.

hooks.name: block_entity_submit
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity_submit( &self, pos: [i32; 3], block: &str, state: BlockStateId, entity: &ModBlockEntity, draw: &mut BlockEntityDraw, )
hooks.doc: Draw the mod block entity at `pos`, of block `block` (`mymod:machine`), on this client: once a frame while it is in view (vanilla's `BlockEntityRenderer.submit`: within 64 blocks, its chunk faded in, and its bounds, `native_block_entity_render_bounding_box`, in the frustum), when its `id` is yours. `state` is the block's state (`blockEntity.getBlockState()`: read its `facing` with `native_block_state_property`), `entity` holds what the server sent (`native_block_entity_update_tag`). Add geometry with `native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_cube`, `native_draw_block` and `native_draw_item` under `draw`'s pose stack, which starts at the block's lower north-west corner, in blocks; `draw` also has the partial tick, the game time and the block's light. API 71.

hooks.name: block_entity_render_bounding_box
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity_render_bounding_box( &self, pos: [i32; 3], block: &str, state: BlockStateId, entity: &ModBlockEntity, bounds: &mut [f32; 6], )
hooks.doc: Where the mod block entity at `pos` draws, for culling (NeoForge's `getRenderBoundingBox`): `bounds` is min x, y, z then max x, y, z, in blocks from the block's lower north-west corner. It starts as the block with a block of margin around it; widen it when your `native_block_entity_submit` draws further (a tall shaft, a beam), or set an infinite value for one never culled. Asked once a frame for each within 64 blocks whose chunk is drawn. API 71.

hooks.name: is_valid_bonemeal_target
hooks.signature: fn native_is_valid_bonemeal_target( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, valid: &mut Option<bool>, )
hooks.doc: A block nothing in Horizon knows a `BonemealableBlock` for is about to take bone meal: vanilla's `BonemealableBlock.isValidBonemealTarget`, `state` the block's own state at `pos`. Answer `valid` for your own blocks: the meal is used up on one as vanilla uses it up (the growth particles and the sound follow, whether or not the roll below grows it), from a player's `BoneMealItem.useOn`, from a dispenser and, on a crop (a villager bonemeals only a `CropBlock`), from a villager. Asked on both sides, as vanilla asks it on both, so a client predicts the use with your answer: say no where you can only grow on a server (`is_client_side`). `Some(false)` refuses the meal, even on a block whose template takes it (vanilla's `growCrop` then keeps the meal); left `None`, the block keeps the `BonemealableBlock` its template gives it, or takes no bone meal. 72.

hooks.name: is_bonemeal_success
hooks.signature: fn native_is_bonemeal_success( &mut self, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, success: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: `BonemealableBlock.isBonemealSuccess` for a block that answered `native_is_valid_bonemeal_target`, after it did: set `success` to grow it this time. Vanilla draws the level's random here (`isBonemealSuccess(Level, RandomSource, BlockPos, BlockState)`), so draw from `native_level_random` to keep vanilla's order. Authoritative servers only. 72.

hooks.name: perform_bonemeal
hooks.signature: fn native_perform_bonemeal( &mut self, ticks: &mut Ticks, dimension: LevelDimension, pos: BlockPos, state: BlockStateId, )
hooks.doc: `BonemealableBlock.performBonemeal` for a block that answered `native_is_valid_bonemeal_target` and whose `native_is_bonemeal_success` said yes: grow it here, `state` its state at `pos`. The meal is used up either way. Change the block with the level's `native_set_block_property`, and schedule with `native_schedule_block_tick` (`ticks` is the hook's). Authoritative servers only. 72.

hooks.name: block_step_on
hooks.signature: fn native_block_step_on( dimension: &str, entity: i32, kind: &str, state: BlockStateId, position: [i32; 3], )
hooks.doc: `Block.stepOn` for a mod block, on its authoritative server level. No self: the simulation owns the entity during this callback.

hooks.name: block_entity_inside
hooks.signature: fn native_block_entity_inside( dimension: &str, entity: i32, kind: &str, state: BlockStateId, position: [i32; 3], )
hooks.doc: `Block.entityInside` for each mod block touched along the entity's movement. Repeated sweep hits in one contact pass are suppressed; idle overlap still fires.

hooks.name: block_fall_on
hooks.signature: fn native_block_fall_on( dimension: &str, entity: i32, kind: &str, state: BlockStateId, position: [i32; 3], distance: f64, damage: &mut f32, )
hooks.doc: `Block.fallOn` for a mod block. Change calculated damage before generic fall sounds and hurt handling; zero prevents both. Creative and fall-immune entities notify with zero damage and retain their immunity. Server-side only.

hooks.name: consume_effect
hooks.signature: fn native_consume_effect(&mut self, kind: &str, data: &serde_json::Value)
hooks.doc: A consumable's effect of a mod's own kind: the item's `on_consume_effects` entry is of a type in a namespace of its own, and the loader kept it for this call. The kind and the JSON the file wrote are here; the acting player is the one consuming, and the game's own effects, sounds, teleports and drops are open. An unclaimed kind does nothing. API 74.

hooks.name: loot_drops
hooks.signature: fn native_loot_drops( &mut self, context: &NativeLootDrops<'_>, drops: &mut Vec<ItemStack>, )
hooks.doc: A block broke or a mob died, and `drops` are the items about to drop, in the order they drop: what the loot tables rolled (after `native_loot_table_load`'s changes), and for a mob what it wore, held or carried (a fox's mouth item, an allay's, piglin's or horse's inventory), but not an enderman's carried block or a copper golem's preserved equipment, which drop after. A charged creeper's head and a fox's mouth item come before the mob's own table. A block's stacks get its block entity's data (a shulker box's items) after this. Add, change or take out stacks; empty ones don't drop (NeoForge's global loot modifiers, Fabric's `LootTableEvents.MODIFY_DROPS`); `context` says what dropped them and how, and it is called even when `drops` is empty. A player's use drops through it too (`NativeLootDrops::used`: shears, a brush, an item frame), with that player named. It hears blocks that a player, an explosion or a mob breaks, not other breaks (leaves decaying, a torch losing its wall, a piston, `/setblock ... destroy`), nor a creative break or a tool that can't harvest the block, nor experience. Server-side, for every player. API 75.

hooks.name: state_for_placement
hooks.signature: fn native_state_for_placement( &self, dimension: LevelDimension, state: BlockStateId, context: &PlacementContext, fluid: FluidState, answer: &mut Option<Option<BlockStateId>>, )
hooks.doc: A block is about to take the state it is placed in (`Block.getStateForPlacement(BlockPlaceContext)`), `state` the block's own default state. Answer only for your blocks: put the state you want in `answer` as `Some(Some(state))` — a state of that block, as vanilla sets properties on its own `defaultBlockState` (another block's is ignored) — or refuse the placement with `Some(None)`: the block goes nowhere and the stack is kept, as vanilla's `null`. Left empty, the block's own placement runs. `context` is vanilla's `BlockPlaceContext` (the clicked face, the placer's rotation, the clicked position, whether the clicked block is being replaced, the item in hand) and `fluid` the fluid in the position the block would go in, which a waterlogged block reads. Build the state from `state` with `native_state_with_property`, and know whether `state` is yours with `native_state_block`. It is asked for every placer that goes through vanilla's placement (a player's `BlockItem.place`, a dispenser's `DirectionalPlaceContext`), and the answer still takes its survival and entity obstruction checks. A trait mod returns `Some(Some(state))` to choose a state, `Some(None)` to refuse, or `None` to leave the answer to the next mod or vanilla. Authoritative servers only. 76.

hooks.name: enchant_effect
hooks.signature: fn native_enchant_effect( &mut self, enchantment: &str, kind: &str, data: &serde_json::Value, level: u32, victim: u32, )
hooks.doc: A `minecraft:post_attack` effect of a mod's own kind, on a mob a player's weapon hit: the entry says `enchanted` attacker and `affected` victim, its `requirements` passed, and its `effect` names a `type` in a namespace outside `minecraft:`. Told the enchantment id, the kind, the `effect` JSON, the level and the mob's id (it may have just died). The acting player is the one whose weapon carries the enchantment. Each such entry is told once a hit, and once for each mob a sweep lands on. A hit on a player, and an entry inside `minecraft:all_of`, aren't told yet. An unclaimed kind does nothing. API 77.

hooks.name: screen_render_post
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_render_post( &self, batch: &mut HudBatch, screen: &NativeScreenView<'_>, )
hooks.doc: The open screen has drawn itself and its tooltips (`Screen.render`, the point of `ScreenEvent.Render.Post`): draw over it with `native_fill`, `native_sprite` and `native_text`, `screen.rect` being its container panel (or the whole window) and `screen.id` the screen it is. Once a frame on the window, never while playing with no screen; `&self`, so it reads and draws only. The Win and Options screens call it on their own path, after their drawing.  It does not fire for the screens drawn over gameplay after it (a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book, a sign editor): those keep `Screen::Playing`, which it skips (the server pack prompt hides an open screen too, and that screen does not fire under it), and draw over what it drew, while vanilla's `ScreenEvent.Render.Post` fires for them. The title's own screens (`title`, `world_select`, `world_create`, `multiplayer`…) fire it too, their `screen.id` from the title state machine and the whole window their `rect` (API 326), and no dialog or prompt over them. API 78.

hooks.name: screen_mouse_button_pressed_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_mouse_button_pressed_pre( &self, screen: &NativeScreenView<'_>, button: i32, modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A mouse button went down over the open screen (`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonPressed.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseClicked`): `screen` is the screen it is, `screen.mouse` where the pointer is (so there is no position of its own), `button` the button's GLFW index (0 left, 1 right, 2 middle, 3 back, 4 forward; a button past those is the platform's own number, which differs between systems) and `modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8). Set `canceled` and the press goes no further: no slot, no screen button, no drag, no hotbar key, no sort or header button.  It fires before anything the screen does with the press, on the window only, and while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (Options and the pack list opened from the title screen count, with no player and no `menu`; the title's own screens since API 326, their `screen.id` from the title state machine). It does not fire on the connect and loading screens, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay, nor while a world loads or saves: the click there stays the game's own. A gamepad click or a click the keyboard's focus sends is not the mouse and fires nothing. API 80.

hooks.name: screen_mouse_button_released_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_mouse_button_released_pre( &self, screen: &NativeScreenView<'_>, button: i32, modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A mouse button went up over the open screen (`ScreenEvent.MouseButtonReleased.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseReleased`), with the same `screen`, `button` and `modifiers` as `native_screen_mouse_button_pressed_pre` and fired at the same point. Set `canceled` and the release goes no further: a pressed slot keeps what it took and no drag, slider or scrollbar lets go.  Cancel a release only when the press it ends was cancelled too: a release the screen took ends the drag or the scroll it began, as it does in vanilla, and no guard here un-cancels it. Same screens as the press; a press that opened another screen ends on that one. API 80.

hooks.name: camera_shake
hooks.signature: fn native_camera_shake(&self, partial: f32, shake: &mut NativeShake)
hooks.doc: The camera shake native mods ask for in this frame, `partial` ticks past the last tick (0 to 1): add your pitch, yaw and roll in degrees and your offset in blocks, along the camera's right, up and back, to `shake`, so several mods' shakes add up. Read while playing only; Horizon scales the sum by Distortion Effects and bounds it (`native_shake_matrix`). API 82.

hooks.name: shader_params
hooks.signature: fn native_shader_params(&self, partial: f32, params: &mut [[f32; 4]; 8])
hooks.doc: The values native mods hand their shader packs in this frame, `partial` ticks past the last tick (0 to 1): a pack's WGSL reads them as `frame.mods` (eight `vec4<f32>`). Write the slots your own pack reads; a mod that bundles its pack as `native-<mod id>` is the one that pack is for. Asked once a frame while a pack is on; a value that isn't finite reads as 0 (`native_shader_params_now`). API 84.

hooks.name: block_highlight
hooks.signature: fn native_block_highlight( &self, pos: [i32; 3], state: BlockStateId, partial: f32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: Before an eligible targeted block's selection outline is built. Cancel skips only the default block highlight, after normal HUD and game-mode gates.

hooks.name: render_hand
hooks.signature: fn native_render_hand( &self, hand: horizon_client::first_person::Hand, stack: Option<&ItemStack>, partial: f32, swing: f32, equip: f32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: Before one first-person hand and its displayed stack are drawn (RenderHandEvent). Equip progress is the inverse arm height, including the item's swap animation scale. Cancel skips that hand's default geometry, including its map and arm geometry. It only hides: the hook has no way to draw a replacement.

hooks.name: client_resources_reloaded
hooks.signature: fn native_client_resources_reloaded(&mut self)
hooks.doc: Render-thread notification after a resource-pack reload has applied successfully. Atlas, models, renderer and client caches already refer to the new resources. Selection/F3+T and server-pack reloads share this point; initial startup does not.

hooks.name: item_decorations
hooks.signature: fn native_item_decorations( &self, stack: &ItemStack, x: f32, y: f32, batch: &mut HudBatch, )
hooks.doc: Append an item's custom decorations after its default bar, cooldown and count. Coordinates are the icon's top-left in GUI units, as the batch takes them; no item translation is active. Runs wherever the shared item-decoration path is used (hotbar, menus, tooltips, and the other screens that draw item icons: advancements, beacon, stats, trading).

hooks.name: use_duration
hooks.signature: fn native_use_duration(&self, stack: &ItemStack, duration: &mut i32)
hooks.doc: `Item.getUseDuration` of `stack`, in ticks: `duration` arrives with vanilla's (a consumable's time, 72000 for a shield, a spear, a bow, 0 for an item with no use over time). A mod's own item (outside `minecraft:`) with no `consumable`, `blocks_attacks` or kinetic weapon that answers above 0 is used over time on a right click, as an `Item.use` that calls `startUsingItem`, until it is let go or the time runs out (`native_living_entity_use_item_finish`). A consumable's time changes too, potions and the other vanilla items keep their own. Asked when a use starts, each tick a mod's item is in use, and each frame the hand draws one in use, on both sides. It has no user, as it is asked so often: answer from the stack alone. API 90.

hooks.name: use_animation
hooks.signature: fn native_use_animation(&self, stack: &ItemStack, animation: &mut UseAnimation)
hooks.doc: `Item.getUseAnimation` of `stack` in use, for the first person hand: `animation` arrives with its consumable's (`eat`, `drink`), else `None`. `Eat` and `Drink` bring the food to the mouth, `Bow` draws, `Trident` raises, `Brush` sweeps; the rest hold the item still. Asked each frame the hand draws an item in use, for an item with no pose of its own (bows, crossbows, tridents, brushes and spears keep theirs). Client-side. API 90.

hooks.name: can_eat
hooks.signature: fn native_can_eat(&self, stack: &ItemStack, can_eat: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: `Player.canEat` for the food `stack`, from `Consumable.canConsume` when eating starts: `can_eat` arrives with vanilla's (creative, `can_always_eat`, or hungry). Clear it to refuse the food, set it to let a full player eat. Both sides (the client starts eating as the server does), so answer from the stack and the player alone. API 90.

hooks.name: living_entity_use_item_start
hooks.signature: fn native_living_entity_use_item_start( &mut self, stack: &ItemStack, entity: Option<i32>, hand: Hand, duration: &mut i32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: NeoForge's `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Start`: `entity` starts using `stack` in `hand` (`LivingEntity.startUsingItem`), for `duration` ticks (`native_use_duration`'s answer). `entity` is a mob's `Entity.getId`, None for a player (`native_acting_player` says who); only players fire it so far. Change `duration` (consumables, potions, spyglasses and mods' items count to it; below 0 refuses the use, and 0 runs it out on its first tick, as `native_living_entity_use_item_tick` running it out, unless the item's own is 0 already), or set `canceled` and the use doesn't start. Both sides, as vanilla's: on the server for every player of the world, and on a server's client for the uses it predicts. Answer the same on both, and change the world only on the server (`native_window` is false there), not on a server's client. API 90.

hooks.name: living_entity_use_item_finish
hooks.signature: fn native_living_entity_use_item_finish( &mut self, stack: &ItemStack, entity: Option<i32>, hand: Hand, duration: i32, result: &mut Option<ItemStack>, )
hooks.doc: NeoForge's `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Finish`: `entity`'s use of `stack` in `hand` ran its time (`LivingEntity.completeUsingItem`), `duration` the ticks left, always 0. `entity` is as in `native_living_entity_use_item_start`. `result` arrives with what `finishUsingItem` left in the hand (the bowl of a stew, none for the last apple; a mod's own item is kept) and may be replaced. Fired for consumables, potions, spyglasses and mods' items. Server-side, for every player of the world (the helpers read the acting one). API 90.

hooks.name: screen_mouse_scrolled_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_mouse_scrolled_pre( &self, screen: &NativeScreenView<'_>, scroll: [f64; 2], modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: The wheel turned over the open screen (`ScreenEvent.MouseScrolled.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.mouseScrolled`): `screen` is the screen it is, `screen.mouse` where the pointer is (so there is no position of its own), `scroll` the wheel's movement in x and y as the game's own scroll handler scales it (a line times the wheel sensitivity: with Discrete Scrolling on, a notch is ±1, its sign only; a touchpad's pixels are divided by 30), and `modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8). Set `canceled` and nothing the screen would scroll moves: not the bundle under the pointer, nor a list, slider, scrollbar or map. Nothing else reads the wheel while a screen of the game's is open, so no hotbar slot changes either.  It fires before the screen scrolls anything, for the window's wheel (horizon-ctl's `scroll-at` sends it through the window too), and while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (Options and the pack list opened from the title screen count, with no player and no `menu`; the title's own since API 326). It does not fire on the connect and loading screens, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay, nor while a world loads or saves: the scroll there stays the game's own. A wheel a gamepad or the keyboard's focus sends is not the mouse and fires nothing. API 93.

hooks.name: player_command
hooks.signature: fn native_player_command( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, command: &str, canceled: &mut bool, replies: &mut Vec<Text>, )
hooks.doc: A command a player typed (NeoForge's `CommandEvent`, before `Commands.performCommand` runs it), without its slash: any command, vanilla's and the mods' own, also one the player may not run. Set `canceled` to stop it: nothing runs and nothing is answered but the lines pushed to `replies`, which go to the player as system chat. No player's state is swapped in and the server's player list is busy with this one, so `native_tell` and the other helpers that take a UUID reach nobody here: answer through `replies`. Once for each command a player sends, on a server, and for each line of a quiet command batch (`horizon:quiet_commands`, whose replies are dropped). A command the server refuses before reading it (unsigned chat arguments, the chat rate limit) never reaches it. 95.

hooks.name: perform_console_command
hooks.signature: fn native_perform_console_command(&mut self, command: &str, ran: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: A command a mod registered, typed on the dedicated server's console or sent through `horizon-server console` (`DedicatedServer.handleConsoleInputs`), without its slash: set `ran` when it is yours. There is no player: the source is the console, at permission level 4, so `native_acting_player` is None and the player-only helpers give nothing; `native_feedback` answers on the console. A name no mod registered goes to vanilla's dispatcher as before. 99.

hooks.name: screen_key_pressed_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_key_pressed_pre( &self, screen: &NativeScreenView<'_>, key: &str, repeat: bool, modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A key went down over the open screen (`ScreenEvent.KeyPressed.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.keyPressed`): `screen` is the screen it is, `key` vanilla's name for the key (`key.keyboard.e`, the name `native_key` hands over) — a key with no name fires nothing — `repeat` whether it is the keyboard's auto-repeat of a held press (Horizon's extra; NeoForge folds repeats into the event), and `modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8). Set `canceled` and the press goes no further: no focus move, no Escape-close, no inventory or hotbar key, no typing by the key itself, no `native_key`.  It fires for the window's presses and their repeats, and for the control socket's `key` (a release fires nothing), after the window's own shortcuts have run — the fullscreen and screenshot keys, the debug keys and the narrator — and while a screen of the game's or the title's is open (Options and the pack list opened from the title screen count, with no player and no `menu`; the title's own since API 326). It does not fire on the connect and loading screens, nor for a server dialog, the server pack, link and code-of-conduct prompts, a book or a sign editor drawn over gameplay, nor while a world loads or saves: the key there stays the game's own. A cancelled press's release still runs, so a `native_key` listener sees that release without its press, and its characters are GLFW's separate char callback and still come; see `native_screen_char_typed_pre`. API 104.

hooks.name: screen_char_typed_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_char_typed_pre( &self, screen: &NativeScreenView<'_>, c: char, modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A character was typed at the open screen (`ScreenEvent.CharacterTyped.Pre`, vanilla's `Screen.charTyped`): `screen` is the screen it is, `c` the character, and `modifiers` GLFW's bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8). Set `canceled` and that one character never reaches a text box.  It fires once per printable character of a key press's text and once per character of the input method's committed text, never for a control character (Enter, Backspace, Tab, Delete, Escape, a Control letter): those are keys, and the game reads them as keys, not as text. A key's characters fire after the key has acted, as GLFW's char callback comes after its key callback (`KeyboardHandler.charTyped`): `screen` is the screen open then, so a key that closes the screen (the inventory key) leaves none to hear its character, where vanilla's closed screen hears nothing, and one that moves the focus types into the box it moved to. They fire even when `native_screen_key_pressed_pre` cancelled the press that carried the text, as NeoForge delivers `CharacterTyped.Pre` for a cancelled `KeyPressed.Pre`: the characters left reach the text box without the key's own effects. Cancelling one character drops only that one. The control socket's `type` fires it too, but not for its `\b` backspace. Same screens as the key press, and it fires with no text box focused (there is nothing to take the character then). API 104.

hooks.name: data_pack_files
hooks.signature: fn native_data_pack_files(&self, files: &mut Vec<(String, Vec<u8>)>)
hooks.doc: The server is assembling its data tables from the world's data packs (`ReloadableServerResources`): a world is opening, or `/reload` was run, and the recipes, tags, loot and advancements are built after this. Push `(path, bytes)` pack files and they join this load. `path` is the overlay's key, `<kind>/<namespace>:<path>` without `.json`, over the kinds the tables read: `recipe/mymod:thing`, `tags/mymod:block/thing`, `loot_table/…`, `advancement/…`, `trade_set/…`, `villager_trade/…`, `dialog/…`. A file that isn't JSON is skipped with a warning. Asked once per load on both paths, so this is where a mod recomputes them. Contributed files sit below the world's own data packs: a pack's file for the same path still overrides a mod's. Server-side (the single player's integrated server included). API 106.

hooks.name: biome_colors
hooks.signature: fn native_biome_colors(&self, biome: &str, colors: &mut BiomeColors)
hooks.doc: Change the colours of `biome` (`minecraft:plains`) on this client: the grass, foliage (leaves, vines), dry foliage (leaf litter) and water tints, 0xRRGGBB, as its biome file and the colormaps set them. Asked for every biome when a mod calls `native_refresh_biome_colors`, which rebuilds the terrain with them; a season mod answers from its season and calls that when the season turns. The dark forest's modifier still applies to the grass set here; the swamp's noise colours replace it. API 107.

hooks.name: server_data_loaded
hooks.signature: fn native_server_data_loaded(&mut self, reload: bool)
hooks.doc: The server's data tables are built (NeoForge's `TagsUpdatedEvent` with `SERVER_DATA_LOAD`): the recipes, tags, loot and advancements of the world's data packs, and the files mods added through `native_data_pack_files`, are what the helpers read from now on. `reload` is false on a world's first open, before its chunks and players are loaded, and true after `/reload` rebuilt them, once the players were sent the new data. The place to drop caches derived from the data and to rebind what depends on it. Server-side (the single player's integrated server included); a client connected to a server never fires it. API 108.

hooks.name: compute_fov
hooks.signature: fn native_compute_fov(&self, partial: f32, camera: [f64; 3], degrees: &mut f32)
hooks.doc: World field of view, after normal calculation and zoom and before projection/Nausea. Called for world rendering and near-plane overlays; hand/HUD FOV uses its own path. Only finite values in 1..=179 degrees replace the computed FOV.

hooks.name: mob_submit
hooks.signature: fn native_mob_submit( &self, mob: &NativeMobRender<'_>, draw: &mut BlockEntityDraw, drawn: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: Draw the mob `mob` (its id, kind, custom name and the frame's body and head turns and walk cycle, `LivingEntityRenderState`) on this client with a model of your own, once a frame while it is in view (vanilla's `EntityRenderer.submit`), and set `drawn` to leave out its vanilla model, armour and held items (NeoForge's `RenderLivingEvent.Pre`, cancelled). Add geometry with `native_draw_cube`, `native_draw_quad`, `native_draw_block` and `native_draw_item` under `draw`'s pose stack, which starts at the mob's feet turned with its body: +z is the way it faces, +x its left, +y up, in blocks. `draw` also has the partial tick, the game time and the mob's light. Its name tag, shadow, flames and glowing outline draw as for any mob. Asked for every mob in view but players; a mob your server half spawned (`native_spawn_mob`) is told apart by its id, sent with mod messages, or by its custom name. A mob is drawn afresh each frame: `draw.keep()` does nothing here. API 110.

hooks.name: camera_distance
hooks.signature: fn native_camera_distance( &self, partial: f32, mirrored: bool, entity: &horizon_client::camera::CameraEntity, distance: &mut f32, )
hooks.doc: Final scaled third-person camera distance, before visual-shape collision clipping. `entity` includes its living scale/distance and optional mount scale/distance. Only finite requests in 0..=1024 blocks replace the vanilla distance.

hooks.name: compute_fog_color
hooks.signature: fn native_compute_fog_color( &self, partial: f32, camera: [f64; 3], fog_type: horizon_client::fog::FogType, rgb: &mut [f32; 3], )
hooks.doc: Computed world fog RGB, after ordinary effects and before upload. Title panoramas skip it. Only finite RGB components in 0..=1 are accepted; alpha and distances stay unchanged.

hooks.name: mouse_button_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_mouse_button_pre( &mut self, button: i32, pressed: bool, modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: Raw mouse button input on any screen, before dispatch; cancel skips dispatch and Post. Button/modifiers use the same GLFW encoding as screen hooks. Synthetic clicks skip it.

hooks.name: mouse_button_post
hooks.signature: fn native_mouse_button_post(&mut self, button: i32, pressed: bool, modifiers: u32)
hooks.doc: An accepted raw button event finished dispatch, including a screen handler's early return.

hooks.name: player_respawned
hooks.signature: fn native_player_respawned(&mut self, player: u128, name: &str)
hooks.doc: `player` (`name`) respawned (NeoForge's `PlayerRespawnEvent`): at the end of `PlayerList.respawn`, once they are placed and their health, food and experience reset, with their state swapped in. Once for each death that ends in a respawn, on a server; not for the End-exit one. 115.

hooks.name: render_fog
hooks.signature: fn native_render_fog( &self, partial: f32, camera: [f64; 3], fog_type: horizon_client::fog::FogType, fog: &mut horizon_client::fog::FogData, )
hooks.doc: Final world fog, after the computed color hook, ordinary calculations and Horizon's fog option, before upload. Title panoramas skip it. Invalid color or distance values retain the original whole fog.

hooks.name: screen_key_released_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_key_released_pre( &self, screen: &NativeScreenView<'_>, key: &str, modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: Before an open screen handles a named key's release (same screen gate as key presses). Cancel bypasses screen handling; physical keys and mapped keyboard hold/toggle state release.

hooks.name: music
hooks.signature: fn native_music(&self, music: &mut Option<Music>, volume: &mut f32)
hooks.doc: Choose this client's music, once a client tick: `music` and `volume` hold what vanilla chose (`Minecraft.getSituationalMusic` and `getMusicVolume`: the biome's track, the creative or underwater one, a boss's, the menu's; None for silence). Set `music` to a track of your own, a sound event of your content mod's `sounds.json` such as `Music::new("mymod:music.spring", 1200, 6000, false)` (the delays in ticks between songs, and whether it cuts off a different song playing), None to keep vanilla's quiet, or change `volume` (0 to 1) to fade it. API 119.

hooks.name: music_layers
hooks.signature: fn native_music_layers(&self, layers: &mut Vec<MusicLayer>)
hooks.doc: The tracks to play over (or instead of) the music on this client, asked once a client tick: push a `MusicLayer` (a sound event, looped, and its volume, 0 to 1) for each. A layer eases to a new volume over up to two seconds, and one left out fades out and stops; layers that first appear in the same tick start together, so list every stem of a piece from the start, the silent ones at volume 0, and raise them (a fuller arrangement as a village grows). Their sound events should be `stream: true` in `sounds.json`. API 119.

hooks.name: datapack_sync
hooks.signature: fn native_datapack_sync(&mut self, recipe_types: &mut Vec<String>)
hooks.doc: The server is about to send its data to the players (NeoForge's `OnDatapackSyncEvent`, its `sendRecipes`): push the recipe types (`minecraft:smelting`, `mymod:crusher`) whose recipes your client half needs. Horizon sends their final recipes — the world's data packs merged, load conditions held — to every Horizon client when it joins and again after each `/reload`; a vanilla client is sent nothing new. Asked once per load, when the server's data tables are built, and the same types go to every player: unlike NeoForge, which asks again for each joining player, it can't differ between players. Push nothing and nothing is sent; push nothing after a load that pushed some and the clients go back to their own recipes. Server-side (the single player's integrated server included). API 120.

hooks.name: recipes_received
hooks.signature: fn native_recipes_received(&mut self, recipe_types: &[String])
hooks.doc: The server's recipes of `recipe_types` arrived (NeoForge's `RecipesReceivedEvent`): from now on the recipe helpers (`native_recipes`, `native_recipes_of_type`) give the server's recipes of those types in place of the window's own, so rebuild what you made of them. It comes after a join, once the window has its player, and after every `/reload`, on a server whose mods asked for them (`native_datapack_sync`), single player included; with no types when the server stopped sending them and the window is back on its own recipes. A recipe the window's own recipe book doesn't know has `book_id` -1. Client-side. API 120.

hooks.name: input_key
hooks.signature: fn native_input_key(&mut self, event: &winit::event::KeyEvent, modifiers: u32)
hooks.doc: A real window key event after handling, including repeats and consumed shortcuts. Receives the original physical/logical key, text, location, state and repeat flag. Modifier bits use the screen hooks' GLFW encoding. Not cancellable.

hooks.name: mouse_scrolling
hooks.signature: fn native_mouse_scrolling( &mut self, scroll: [f64; 2], accumulated: [i32; 2], buttons: [bool; 3], cursor: [f32; 2], modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: Gameplay scrolling after whole steps accumulate, before hotbar/spectator handling. `scroll` is scaled x/y, `accumulated` whole x/y steps, `buttons` left/middle/right, and `cursor` the GUI position. Cancel skips gameplay scrolling; synthetic input skips it.

hooks.name: screen_mouse_dragged_pre
hooks.signature: fn native_screen_mouse_dragged_pre( &self, screen: &NativeScreenView<'_>, button: i32, delta: [f32; 2], modifiers: u32, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: Before a real held-button movement reaches screen drag handlers. `screen.mouse` is the current GUI position; `delta` is its GUI-space movement. Cancel keeps the new cursor position but skips all screen drag handlers.

hooks.name: mod_container_viewers
hooks.signature: fn native_mod_container_viewers( &mut self, dimension: &str, pos: [i32; 3], viewers: u32, previous: u32, )
hooks.doc: The number of players with the mod container at `pos` of `dimension` open went from `previous` to `viewers` (vanilla's `ContainerOpenersCounter`, as a barrel keeps it): 0 to more than 0 is `onOpen`, back to 0 is `onClose`, any change `openerCountChanged`, so a block can show itself open while `viewers` is not 0. Counted every tick from the players' open menus, so a player who leaves without closing (a lost connection, death, another dimension, out of reach, the block gone) is heard too (`recheckOpeners`). Once for each change, with no player's state swapped in. Server-side. 124.

hooks.name: living_knockback
hooks.signature: fn native_living_knockback( entity: i32, kind: &str, damage_type: &str, causing: i32, direct: i32, strength: &mut f64, x: &mut f64, z: &mut f64, canceled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: `LivingEntity.knockback` is about to push entity `entity` of type `kind` (`minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:player`) `strength` away from the direction (`x`, `z`), on the raw strength, before the entity's knockback resistance takes its share and its motion changes (docs/native-mods.md, API 125). Vanilla's direction points at the source of a hit (the attacker's side), and the entity is pushed the other way. Change `strength`, `x` or `z`, or set `canceled`, and the push follows them: canceled, the entity's motion is left alone. A `strength` of 0 or less after the hook is no push, and a direction too short to tell draws a random one after it, as in vanilla. A value a mod leaves that is not a finite number is put back as it was. `damage_type` (`minecraft:player_attack`), `causing` (`DamageSource.getEntity`) and `direct` (`getDirectEntity`) are the push's `DamageSource`, named as `native_living_incoming_damage` names a hit's, with the same entity ids left at 0. It fires for the players and mobs the game knocks back: a hit's own push, a sprinting or Knockback hit, a sweep, a spear, a shield's push on its holder and a goat's ram. It does not fire for a sulfur cube with a block that a hit with a causing entity knocks back (`SulfurCube.knockback` does not call `super` there), for the pushes vanilla doesn't make with `LivingEntity.knockback` (the ender dragon's wings, Punch arrows, explosions, wind charges, a mace smash's area, a hoglin's throw), nor yet for the ones Horizon makes another way: a mob's melee push from its attack knockback or a Knockback weapon, an armor stand's, the ender dragon's. It runs on the thread that ticks the world (the server thread): state shared with render thread hooks needs synchronising. No `self`: the game is in the middle of the hit. API 125.

hooks.name: experience_orb_can_merge

Server-side. API 128.

Set `canceled` to stop it: both orbs stay, and a spawning orb tries the next orb in reach, then spawns on its own. Server-side. API 128.

hooks.name: living_entity_use_item_tick
hooks.signature: fn native_living_entity_use_item_tick( &mut self, stack: &ItemStack, entity: Option<i32>, hand: Hand, duration: &mut i32, canceled: &mut bool, )

Change `duration` to move the end (consumables, potions, spyglasses and mods' items count to it, and so do a client's eating crumbs and first person pose, as the started duration of `native_living_entity_use_item_start` does). A cancel sets it to -1. Once a mod set it, the use goes on only while it is above 0: at 0 or less, by a cancel or set, the item's tick is skipped and the server finishes the use (`completeUsingItem`: `finishUsingItem`, the food eaten, `native_living_entity_use_item_finish`), while an item used on release (a crossbow) stays frozen until let go. NeoForge's javadoc says a cancel stops the use, but its code finishes it; this follows the code. On a server's client a run-out use stays in use, frozen, so letting go still tells the server. Both sides, as vanilla's `updatingUsingItem`: answer the same on both, and change the world only on the server (`native_window` is false there), not on a server's client. Runs every tick of every use: check the item first. API 131.

It comes where `ItemStack.onUseTick` calls the item, once `native_living_entity_use_item_tick` let the use go on: after a consumable's crumbs, for consumables, shields and mods' items (vanilla's other items do their own, and a kinetic weapon has none on the server). Both sides, as `native_living_entity_use_item_tick`: change the world only where this `Game` runs the world, not on a server's client. Runs every tick of every use: check the item first. API 131.

hooks.name: living_entity_use_item_stop

hooks.doc: NeoForge's `LivingEntityUseItemEvent.Stop`: `entity` lets go of `stack` in `hand` before its use ran its time (`LivingEntity.releaseUsingItem`: the use button let go, a screen opened), `duration` the ticks left. Set `canceled` to skip the item's release (a bow doesn't shoot, a spyglass makes no sound, `native_release_using` isn't called); the use stops anyway. Not when the hand changed item, which stops the use without a release. Both sides, as `native_living_entity_use_item_tick`. API 131.

Once for each open: `native_level_unload` follows. Server-side. API 134.

Client-side, on the window; the server's levels have `native_level_load`. API 135.

hooks.signature: fn native_client_level_unload(&mut self, dimension: &str)

hooks.name: hears_projectile_impacts

Asked once a server tick before the projectiles fly; only then does the tick keep the copy of each flying projectile that a canceled impact flies on from, so a game without such a mod pays nothing. Server-side. API 136.

hooks.name: projectile_impact
hooks.signature: fn native_projectile_impact( &mut self, dimension: &str, projectile: u32, kind: &str, owner: u32, entity: Option<u32>, entity_kind: &str, block: [i32; 3], face: [i32; 3], at: [f64; 3], canceled: &mut bool, )

It hit the entity `entity` of type `entity_kind` (a player is `minecraft:player`; a dragon's part is `minecraft:ender_dragon`), or, with `entity` None, the block at `block` on its `face` (the face's normal, `[0, 1, 0]` for the top), at the point `at`. Covers what `tick_projectiles` flies: arrows, tridents, snowballs, eggs, pearls, potions, fireballs, wither skulls, wind charges, llama spit and shulker bullets, from players, mobs and dispensers. It does not fire for a breeze's deflection, for a hit on a wind charge, for fireworks or for fishing bobbers. A dragon part or End crystal is told by the id of the dragon or crystal. Heard only when a mod also sets `native_hears_projectile_impacts`. Server-side. API 136.

hooks.doc: Whether a mod listens to `native_player_submit` or `native_mob_layer`: a mod that hooks either hooks this one too and sets `listened` (HEAD, `*listened = true`). Without it the game poses no player or mob for them, each frame. Client-side. API 149.

hooks.name: sign_changed

hooks.signature: fn native_standalone_models(models: &mut Vec<String>)
hooks.doc: Models no blockstate names that this client bakes beside the block models (NeoForge's `ModelEvent.RegisterStandalone`): push their ids (`mymod:block/shaft_half`, the model at `assets/mymod/models/block/shaft_half.json`).
