hooks.name: menu_quick_move
hooks.neoforge: none (a Java menu overrides AbstractContainerMenu.quickMoveStack; no event)
hooks.signature: fn native_menu_quick_move( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], entity: &mut ModBlockEntity, container_slots: usize, slot: usize, stack: &mut ItemStack, handled: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player shift-clicked slot `slot` of the menu of the mod block entity at `pos` (`AbstractContainerMenu.quickMoveStack`, the method a Java menu overrides), on the server, before the game's own routing: move the stack where your block wants it. `slot` is the menu's index: below `container_slots` it is the block's own slot (`entity.items`), from there on the player's inventory (27 main slots, then the hotbar). `stack` is a copy of what the slot holds; take what you move out of it (put it in `entity.items`, or in another block with `native_insert_item`) and set `handled`: the slot then holds what is left of `stack` (whatever you wrote to that slot of `entity.items`), the game's routing is skipped, and the player's client gets the menu again. Left unhandled, `entity.items` goes back to what it held and the game moves the stack as for any container; a later mod sees what an earlier one did to `stack`.  For a mod container on a vanilla menu type and on a mod menu type, the left or right button, a slot that holds something and that the mod's screen shows; not for a spectator or a dead player, a menu no longer valid, nor during a drag. Asked once per click, where vanilla asks `quickMoveStack` again while it keeps moving the same item. The player's state is swapped in, so `native_acting_player` names them; `entity` is out of the world during the call, as in `native_menu_button`. API 309.

Not heard: a dispenser, a cauldron, and a fluid a block places itself. 179.

hooks.name: container_opened
hooks.neoforge: none (NeoForge's PlayerContainerEvent.Open fires after the menu is open and is not cancellable)
hooks.signature: fn native_container_opened( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, kind: &str, pos: Option<[i32; 3]>, cancel: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A player opens one of the game's own menus (`ServerPlayer.openMenu`; the job of NeoForge's `PlayerContainerEvent.Open`, which comes after the menu is open and cannot stop it): `kind` is the menu type (`minecraft:generic_9x3`, `minecraft:furnace`, `minecraft:crafting`, `minecraft:merchant`, `minecraft:anvil`, `minecraft:lectern`...; a horse's inventory is `minecraft:horse_inventory`) and `pos` the block it belongs to, none for a villager, a mount or a vehicle's chest. Heard after the checks that refuse the menu (a locked container, a spectator) and before the menu that was open closes. Set `cancel` and nothing opens: the open menu stays as it was and the click is spent. The player's state is swapped in for the call, as for `native_perform_command`, so `native_acting_player`, `native_tell` and the item helpers reach them. Not heard: a menu a mod opens (`native_open_menu`), the inventory screen, and the editors (sign, book, command block). Server-side, for every player of the world. 176.

hooks.name: creative_slot
hooks.signature: fn native_creative_slot( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, slot: i32, item: &str, count: i32, cancel: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A creative-mode player sets a slot of their inventory from the creative screen (`ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handleSetCreativeModeSlot`): `slot` is the inventory menu's slot (5 to 8 armour, 9 to 35 the inventory, 36 to 44 the hotbar, 45 the off hand; below 0 is a stack thrown out of the screen, which is dropped) and `item` (`minecraft:air` for an emptied slot) and `count` what is put there. Heard once the packet passed vanilla's checks (a creative player, a real slot, a valid stack) and before the slot changes or the stack drops. Set `cancel` and the packet is ignored. The player's state is swapped in for the call, as for `native_perform_command`, so `native_acting_player`, `native_tell` and the item helpers reach them. Not heard: stacks a creative player gets other ways (middle-click pick block, `/give`). Server-side, for every player of the world. 177.

hooks.name: food_level_changed
hooks.signature: fn native_food_level_changed( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, from: i32, to: &mut i32, cancel: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: The food level of the server player `player` (`name`) is about to change from `from` to `to` (Bukkit's `FoodLevelChangeEvent`): eating, hunger and saturation effects, the exhaustion that costs a point, starving. Change `to` (kept between 0 and 20; saturation never exceeds it) or set `cancel` to leave the level at `from`, saturation included. Heard once for the change a player's turn made as a whole, so two changes in one tick arrive as one. Not heard: the full food bar a respawn gives, the food a player joins with and the host of a LAN world. The player's state is swapped in, so `native_acting_player`, `native_tell` and the item helpers reach them. On a server. 169.

hooks.name: hanging_break
hooks.signature: fn native_hanging_break( &mut self, player: Option<u128>, kind: &str, pos: [i32; 3], cancel: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: An item frame (`minecraft:item_frame`, `minecraft:glow_item_frame`) or a painting (`minecraft:painting`), `kind` its entity type and `pos` the block it hangs in, is about to break: a server player's hit (`player`, their state swapped in, so `native_tell` answers them), a blast, or the wall it hangs on gone (`player` None for both). Where `BlockAttachedEntity.hurtServer` and its survival check would kill it, before anything drops or sounds. Set `cancel` and it stays, as it was. A hit that only takes the item out of a frame does not break the frame and is not asked. The game's own player's hit is not asked, nor is `/kill`. 319.

hooks.name: hanging_place
hooks.signature: fn native_hanging_place( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, kind: &str, pos: [i32; 3], cancel: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A server player places a hanging entity: an item frame (`minecraft:item_frame`, `minecraft:glow_item_frame`), a painting (`minecraft:painting`) or a leash knot (`minecraft:leash_knot`, when a lead is tied to a fence that has none yet), `kind` its entity type and `pos` the block it takes (the fence's for a knot). Where `HangingEntityItem.useOn` and `LeadItem.useOn` create it, once it is known to fit and before anything is placed or used up. Set `cancel` and nothing is placed: the item stays in the player's hand. The player's state is swapped in, so `native_tell` answers them. Only for guests of a server; `/summon`, a dispenser and the game's own player are not heard, nor is a lead tied to a mob or a boat. 180.

hooks.name: item_damaged
hooks.neoforge: none (vanilla: ItemStack.hurtAndBreak; PlayerDestroyItemEvent is only the break)
hooks.signature: fn native_item_damaged( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, item: &str, amount: &mut i32, cancel: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: The item `item` of a server player is about to lose `amount` points of durability (`ItemStack.hurtAndBreak`; Bukkit's `PlayerItemDamageEvent`): the tool that mines or hits, the armour that takes a hit, a shield, a rod, an elytra. `amount` is what is left after Unbreaking; change it (0 or less leaves the item whole) or set `cancel` for no wear at all. It is not heard for a creative player's tools (they take no wear) nor when Unbreaking already saved the item, nor for the wear of a mob's armour or of a tool a dispenser uses, nor the host of a LAN world. The player's state is swapped in, so `native_acting_player`, `native_tell` and the item helpers reach them. Once for each wear, on a server. 162.

hooks.name: player_changed_dimension
hooks.signature: fn native_player_changed_dimension( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, from: &str, to: &str, )
hooks.doc: `player` (`name`) changed dimension (NeoForge's `PlayerChangedDimensionEvent`): `from` and `to` are dimension ids (`minecraft:overworld`, `minecraft:the_nether`, `minecraft:the_end`). Heard once per move, when it has ended: the portal's exit is found and the player stands there (after the destination has loaded), a command's teleport has landed, or a respawn in another level than the death's is placed for good (a bed or anchor, or the world spawn's free column, after the fallback when a respawn block was gone). The level of `to` is the one in place, and the player's state is swapped in, as for `native_perform_command`: `native_acting_player`, `native_tell`, the item helpers and the rest reach them. Heard for: Nether and End portals (also riding a vehicle, and leaving the End as its winner), `/execute in ... run tp` and any other command that teleports a player into another level, and the death respawn. Not heard: a move within a level (`/tp`, an End gateway), a player who leaves before the move ends, a move that ends where it started (a respawn in the dimension of the death), and anything outside a dedicated server. 154.

hooks.name: player_clone
hooks.signature: fn native_player_clone(&mut self, player: u128, name: &str, was_death: bool)
hooks.doc: A player's data was copied to their new player (NeoForge's `PlayerEvent.Clone`, from `ServerPlayer.restoreFrom`): `was_death` is true after a death, false when they left the End after the credits (`respawn` with `keepAllPlayerData`). The uuid stays the same, so the old and the new player share `player`. Heard before the new player is placed, on a server, with no player's state swapped in. Not cancellable.

hooks.name: player_commands_sent
hooks.signature: fn native_player_commands_sent( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, names: &mut Vec<String>, )
hooks.doc: The command tree a server sends a player (NeoForge's and Paper's "commands sent to a player" stage): when they join and when their level changes (`/op`, `/deop`, the LAN settings). `names` are the root commands their client would get, vanilla's they may use and the mods'; take a name out and that client gets the tree without it (and without what it leads to), so it neither completes nor highlights it. This hides the command from the client only: the server still runs a typed one, `native_player_command` stops it. For a player who is already on, their state is swapped in and the helpers (`native_tell`...) work; for one who is joining it is not, and their client has no world to tell yet. The tree the hub sends again by itself (after a respawn or a change of level) keeps the last answer and does not ask again; the integrated server's owner is not asked when the world's cheats are switched. 171.

hooks.neoforge: none (NeoForge's PlayerDestroyItemEvent carries the original stack and a hand, which armour has not; this hook only listens and names the slot instead. Bukkit's PlayerItemBreakEvent)
hooks.signature: fn native_player_destroy_item( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, item: &str, slot: &str, )
hooks.doc: The item `item` of the server player `player` (`name`) broke in `slot` (`mainhand`, `offhand`, `head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet`, `body` or `saddle`): `LivingEntity.onEquippedItemBroken`, Bukkit's `PlayerItemBreakEvent`. Listen only; armour has a slot, not a hand. The player's state is swapped in. Once for each break, on a server; a creative player and the host of a LAN world are not heard. 315.

hooks.name: player_fish
hooks.neoforge: none (NeoForge's ItemFishedEvent fires after the loot roll, in FishingHook.retrieve; Bukkit's PlayerFishEvent)
hooks.signature: fn native_player_fish( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, state: i32, cancel: &mut bool, )
hooks.doc: A server player's fishing rod, with `state`: 0 the cast (`FishingRodItem.use` throwing the bobber), 1 a fish biting (`FishingHook.catchingFish`), 2 the reel-in of a bite, which gives the catch, 3 the reel-in with nothing on the line, 4 the reel-in of a bobber hooked to an entity or item (like Bukkit's `PlayerFishEvent`; NeoForge's `ItemFishedEvent` is later, in `FishingHook.retrieve`). Set `cancel` on the cast and nothing is thrown; on a bite the fish gets away and the wait starts over; on a reel-in (2 to 4) nothing happens, the bobber stays out and the rod takes no wear. The bobber ending by itself (too far, the rod put away, the owner dying), nor the host of a LAN world's rod. The player's state is swapped in, so `native_acting_player`, `native_tell` and the item helpers reach them. Once for each cast, bite and reel-in, on a server. 160.

hooks.name: player_flower_pot_manipulate
hooks.signature: fn native_player_flower_pot_manipulate( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, pos: [i32; 3], plant: &str, )

hooks.signature: fn native_player_game_mode_changed( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, from: i32, to: i32, cancel: &mut bool, )

For a change the game makes inside a player's turn their state is swapped in; for the hardcore respawn it is not. 158.

hooks.doc: Mending repaired a server player's item with experience from an orb. `repair` is durability restored and `experience` is the orb's value. Helpers looking up the guest through `self.lan` may find nothing during packet handling. Server-side. 241.

hooks.name: player_lectern_page_change
hooks.signature: fn native_player_lectern_page_change( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, pos: [i32; 3], page: i32, )
hooks.doc: A server player changed the page of a lectern, after its page and redstone pulse changed. `page` is the zero-based new page. Helpers looking up a guest through `self.lan` may find nothing during packet handling. Server-side. 242.

hooks.name: player_load_from_file
hooks.signature: fn native_player_load_from_file( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, directory: &std::path::Path, )
hooks.doc: A player was loaded from the world's save (NeoForge's `PlayerEvent.LoadFromFile`, `PlayerList.loadPlayerData`): their `.dat` has been read and applied, and they are not placed in a level yet. `directory` is the world's player directory (`players/data`): a mod reads its own file there, named `<uuid>.<suffix>` as `getPlayerFile(suffix)` names it. hooks.name: player_login
hooks.neoforge: none (Bukkit's PlayerLoginEvent; NeoForge's PlayerNegotiationEvent is not cancellable)
hooks.signature: fn native_player_login( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, cancel: &mut bool, reason: &mut Option<Text>, )
hooks.doc: A player whose login the server has accepted (NeoForge's `PlayerNegotiationEvent` stage): the name, whitelist, ban and server-full checks have passed and the player holds a place, but their saved state is not loaded and they are not placed in a level yet. Set `cancel` to refuse them: they are disconnected with `reason` (a plain "Disconnected" if it is left unset) and nothing else of the join (the join message, `native_player_logged_in`) happens. Once for each player who joins, on a server. The player is not placed yet and their client has no world to show a message in, so no player's state is swapped in and `native_tell` reaches nobody: the refusal `reason` is the answer. The checks that need no mod (name, whitelist, bans, a full server, the proxy's forwarding) refuse earlier, on the connection, and this hook does not hear those players. 172.

hooks.name: player_save_to_file
hooks.signature: fn native_player_save_to_file( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, directory: &std::path::Path, )
hooks.doc: A player was saved to the world's store (NeoForge's `PlayerEvent.SaveToFile`, `PlayerList.save`): when they leave or the world closes, when a dedicated or integrated server saves its guests, and for an integrated server's owner when the world saves them. Once for each save. `directory` is the world's player directory (`players/data`): write your own file there, named `<uuid>.<suffix>`, never the player's `.dat`. The player may be leaving, so no player's state is swapped in. Not cancellable. Autosave snapshots are written asynchronously: this notification runs on a later server tick after a successful write, possibly after WorldSaved. Live state may have advanced beyond the saved snapshot; a process exit before completions are drained can prevent notification delivery.

hooks.name: player_sprint
hooks.signature: fn native_player_sprint(&mut self, player: u128, name: &str, sprinting: bool)
hooks.doc: A server player's sprint started or stopped: their client sent `START_SPRINTING` or `STOP_SPRINTING` (the sprint key, a double tap forward, or letting go) and the server's player is now `sprinting` (vanilla's `setSprinting` in `handlePlayerCommand`). Heard only when it changes. It cannot be stopped, and it hears what the client asks, not what the server does: a sprint that ends by itself (a hit's knockback, hunger, a wall) is not reported. The player's state is swapped in, so the helpers and `native_tell` work. Once for each change, on a server. 173.

hooks.name: player_swap_hands
hooks.signature: fn native_player_swap_hands(&mut self, player: u128, name: &str, cancel: &mut bool)
hooks.doc: `player` (`name`) pressed the swap-hands key: heard before the main and off hand items swap (the `SWAP_ITEM_WITH_OFFHAND` player action that `ServerGamePacketListenerImpl.handlePlayerAction` answers; Bukkit's `PlayerSwapHandItemsEvent`), not for a spectator. Set `cancel` to keep the items where they are: the player's client, which swapped them at once, gets its slots back. The player's state is swapped in, so `native_acting_player`, `native_tell` and the item helpers reach them. Once for each press, on a server. Not heard: the same swap made in an open inventory (hovering a slot and pressing the key, a menu click) and the host of a LAN world. 168.

hooks.name: player_take_lectern_book
hooks.signature: fn native_player_take_lectern_book( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, pos: [i32; 3], book: &str, )
hooks.doc: A server player took the book from a lectern, after the menu and block entity changed. `book` is the removed item id. Helpers looking up a guest through `self.lan` may find nothing during packet handling. Server-side. 243.

hooks.name: player_teleported
hooks.neoforge: none (EntityTeleportEvent.TeleportCommand fires before the move and can cancel it; this hook is told after the move)
hooks.signature: fn native_player_teleported( &mut self, player: u128, name: &str, from: [f64; 3], to: [f64; 3], dimension: &str, )

hooks.name: menu_extra_data
hooks.signature: fn native_menu_extra_data( &mut self, player: u128, menu: &str, block: &str, pos: [i32; 3], data: &mut Option<Vec<u8>>, )
hooks.doc: Block `block` at `pos` opens its mod menu type `menu` for server player `player`: set `data` to hand the menu's screen bytes of your own (a machine's tier, mode or recipes), up to 32 KiB, which the client reads with `native_screen_extra_data` while the screen is open (NeoForge's `openMenu` with an extra-data writer). The first mod to set it wins, so answer only for your blocks. The player's state is not swapped in. 401.

hooks.name: merchant_offer_traded
hooks.neoforge: none (NeoForge has no such event; Bukkit's PlayerTradeEvent#getTrade is mutable)
hooks.signature: fn native_merchant_offer_traded( &mut self, merchant: u32, kind: &str, offer: &mut MerchantOffer, )
hooks.doc: A trade of a villager or a wandering trader was made and its `offer` (the live one in the trading session, not a copy) is in the state the trade left it in: `uses` counted. A mod may change it (Bukkit's `PlayerTradeEvent#getTrade` is mutable): `uses`, `max_uses`, `demand`, `special_price_diff`, `price_multiplier`, `xp`. The change stands: the next click and the offers sent to the player see it. Once per trade (a shift-click that trades several times asks for each trade only after the click, so the stock it ran down in that click is not given back before the click ends), before the trade's statistic and `trade_with_villager`, which hear the offer as the trade left it. `merchant` is the trader's entity id, `kind` its type. Not asked for a trade window without a trader. Server-side. API 406.

hooks.name: add_server_reload_listeners
hooks.signature: fn native_add_server_reload_listeners( &mut self, listeners: &mut Vec<NativeReloadListener>, )
hooks.doc: The folders of JSON files native mods read from the data (`AddServerReloadListenersEvent`): push yours, each a listener id and a folder under `data/<namespace>/`. Asked at the start of every data load of a server: a world opening, `/reload`. A folder that leaves `data/<namespace>/` is skipped. API 400.

hooks.name: server_reload_listener_apply
hooks.signature: fn native_server_reload_listener_apply( &mut self, listener: &NativeReloadListener, files: &[(String, serde_json::Value)], )
hooks.doc: A listener's files were read (`SimpleJsonResourceReloadListener`'s `apply`): `files` holds `<namespace>:<path>` (the file's path under the folder, without `.json`) and its JSON, sorted by id, from the resource root (vanilla's and content mods' data) and the world's enabled data packs; for each id the top pack's file, and a file that isn't JSON is logged and left out. Every mod hears every listener, so check `listener.id`. Fired on each data load before `native_server_data_loaded`. Server-side. API 400.

hooks.name: client_start
hooks.signature: fn native_client_start(&mut self)
hooks.doc: Client initialization, before any outgoing connection; a window need not exist yet.

hooks.name: client_disconnecting
hooks.signature: fn native_client_disconnecting(&self)
hooks.doc: Before an actual connection is discarded, not on a dimension change. NeoForge's `ClientPlayerNetworkEvent.LoggingOut`, told here after `native_client_level_unload` and only when a connection ends.

hooks.name: client_stopping
hooks.signature: fn native_client_stopping(&self)
hooks.doc: Once before this client's final save/exit. A mod can flush and join its worker here.

hooks.name: menu_background
hooks.signature: fn native_menu_background(&self, radius: &mut Option<f32>)
hooks.doc: The normal menu blur request, before finite/range validation. None disables it.

hooks.name: gui_render_post
hooks.neoforge: RenderGuiEvent.Post (after the whole GUI, open screens included; also under F1, which gui_hidden tells)
hooks.signature: fn native_gui_render_post( &self, batch: &mut HudBatch, gui_hidden: bool, focused: bool, )
hooks.doc: After the complete normal GUI batch, including screens, prompts, toasts, debug overlays, the pad cursor and IME. Fires even with F1 or a menu open; file/world loading and resource-reload overlays do not fire it. The batch is in GUI pixels. `native_camera` is this frame's world camera (None on the panorama). `gui_hidden` is the effective HUD mode; `focused` is window focus. A mod decides whether its foreground indicator respects those flags. Client only; the host is read-only. API 410.

hooks.name: world_hold
hooks.signature: fn native_world_hold(&self, hold: &mut WorldHold)
hooks.doc: Whether native mods hold the terrain's picture this frame: call `hold.hold()` to keep every section drawn as it is while the world changes under it, or `hold.hold_within(x, z, radius)` for only the sections inside circles. Not asking lets go, and every change shows on that frame. Asked once a frame while a world is shown, before the frame's section uploads, by each player's game (splitscreen: each its own). Client only. API 414.

helpers.name: draw_quad
helpers.signature: fn native_draw_quad( &self, draw: &mut BlockEntityDraw, sprite: &str, corners: [[f32; 3]; 4], uv: [f32; 4], tint: u32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Draws a quad with `corners` in blocks under `draw`'s pose, in a model face's order (top left, bottom left, bottom right, top right as seen from its front), textured with the `uv` rectangle (u0, v0, u1, v1 in texels of 16 per side) of `sprite` (`mymod:entity/screen`, `mymod:block/casing`, `block/stone`) times the 0xRRGGBB `tint` (0xFFFFFF for none). False for an unknown sprite. API 71.

helpers.name: draw_cube
helpers.signature: fn native_draw_cube( &self, draw: &mut BlockEntityDraw, from: [f32; 3], to: [f32; 3], faces: [Option<CubeFace<'_>>; 6], tint: u32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Draws a box from `from` to `to` (texels of 16 per block, as a block model's element) under `draw`'s pose, with the faces given, by `Direction` (down, up, north, south, west, east), baked as a model element's are (`FaceBakery`), times the 0xRRGGBB `tint`. A turned box is drawn under a turned pose (`BlockEntityDraw::rotate_about`). False when a face's sprite is unknown; that face is left out. API 71.

helpers.name: draw_block
helpers.signature: fn native_draw_block( &self, draw: &mut BlockEntityDraw, block: &str, properties: &[(&str, &str)], ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Draws block `block`'s model (`mymod:cog`, any block with a model) in the state with `properties` (`[("axis", "x")]`, the rest default) under `draw`'s pose, as vanilla's `submitBlockModel` draws a block in an entity's place: a block's baked model, with its default tints. A moving part that is no block is a standalone model (`native_draw_model`). False for an unknown block or property. API 71.

helpers.name: draw_item
helpers.signature: fn native_draw_item( &self, draw: &mut BlockEntityDraw, stack: &ItemStack, display: DisplayContext, owner_yaw: Option<f32>, seed: i32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Draws `stack` under `draw`'s pose as an item is drawn in the world (`ItemModelResolver.updateForTopItem` and `ItemStackRenderState.submit`), centred on the pose's origin, in its model's `display` transform: `Fixed` as a campfire's or an item frame's, `Ground` as a dropped item's. `seed` picks among random models (a campfire passes its slot plus its position's hash). `owner_yaw` makes the block entity the item's owner (`ItemOwner`), at the block's centre and turned that many degrees (`getVisualRotationYInDegrees`), as a shelf is: a compass on it points to its target from there. None draws it with no owner, as a campfire does. False for an empty stack or one with no model. The client's copy of a block entity has no item slots (`entity.items` is empty there): send the stacks you draw in `native_block_entity_update_tag` and read them from `entity.nbt`. API 91.

helpers.name: attachments
helpers.signature: fn native_attachments( &mut self, holder: Holder, ) -> AttachmentResult<&mut Attachments>
helpers.doc: Access a server-owned holder's attachment map. On a client it is the copy of what the server synced: `set` and `remove` change only the copy.

helpers.name: teleport_mob
helpers.signature: fn native_teleport_mob(&mut self, dimension: &str, id: u32, pos: [f64; 3]) -> bool
helpers.doc: Moves mob `id` to `pos` at once, as `/tp` does: it dismounts, drops its path and resets its fall. False for no such mob, another dimension or a position outside `/summon`'s bounds. API 37.

helpers.name: push_mob
helpers.signature: fn native_push_mob(&mut self, dimension: &str, id: u32, velocity: [f64; 3]) -> bool
helpers.doc: Adds `velocity` to mob `id`'s: false for no such mob, another dimension or a velocity that isn't finite. API 37.

helpers.name: set_mob_health
helpers.signature: fn native_set_mob_health(&mut self, dimension: &str, id: u32, health: f32) -> bool
helpers.doc: Sets the living mob `id`'s health, cut to its maximum: false for no such mob, another dimension or a health that isn't above 0 (`native_kill_mob` kills). API 37.

helpers.name: kill_mob
helpers.signature: fn native_kill_mob(&mut self, dimension: &str, id: u32) -> bool
helpers.doc: Kills mob `id` as `/kill` does: it falls and drops its loot. False for no such living mob or another dimension. API 37.

helpers.name: remove_mob
helpers.signature: fn native_remove_mob(&mut self, dimension: &str, id: u32) -> bool
helpers.doc: Takes mob `id` out of the world with no death and no loot: false for no such mob or another dimension. API 37.

helpers.name: summon
helpers.signature: fn native_summon( &mut self, dimension: &str, kind: &str, pos: [f64; 3], nbt: Compound, ) -> Option<u32>
helpers.doc: Spawns an entity of `kind` (`minecraft:item_display`) at `pos` in the level in place, `dimension`, from `nbt` (its compound, as `/summon <kind> <pos> <nbt>` takes it; passengers included): its id. None on a client's copy of the world, for a position outside `/summon`'s bounds, a chunk that isn't loaded, a kind Horizon can't load, or one a mod kept out (`native_entity_join_level`). API 59. Since API @API:npc_any_level@, `dimension` may be any level the server has loaded, which is put in place for the summon (`execute in <dimension> run summon`); a level not loaded is refused.

helpers.name: move_entity
helpers.signature: fn native_move_entity( &mut self, dimension: &str, id: u32, pos: [f64; 3], yaw: f32, pitch: f32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Moves entity `id`, one Horizon keeps without simulating (a display, a marker, an interaction), to `pos` facing `yaw` and `pitch` in degrees; a display eases there over its `teleport` ticks. False for no such entity, another dimension or a position outside `/summon`'s bounds. Mobs move with `native_teleport_mob`. API 59.

helpers.name: remove_entity
helpers.signature: fn native_remove_entity(&mut self, dimension: &str, id: u32) -> bool
helpers.doc: Removes entity `id`, one Horizon keeps without simulating, as `/kill` does (it drops nothing and isn't saved). False for no such entity or another dimension. Mobs go with `native_remove_mob`. API 59. Since API @API:remove_projectiles@ it also takes projectiles (arrows, tridents, snowballs, eggs, pearls, fireballs, wind charges, llama spit, shulker bullets, firework rockets) as `/kill` does, and a server player's fishing bobber (`Entity.discard`; the player in place's, or, outside a guest's turn, any of this level's players').

helpers.name: lit_block_name
helpers.doc: Read a loaded, light-emitting block. No implicit chunk loading.

helpers.name: flame_particle
helpers.signature: fn native_flame_particle(&mut self, at: [f64; 3], soul: bool)
helpers.doc: A small local vanilla particle; caller should rate-limit emission.

helpers.name: carried_stack
helpers.signature: fn native_carried_stack(&mut self, slot: i32) -> Option<&mut ItemStack>
helpers.doc: The stack the acting player carries in `slot`, by `native_inventory_tick`'s numbers: none for an empty slot or another number. Change it as you like: a count of 0 empties the slot at the end of `native_inventory_tick`, and the player's client gets the change. API 39.

helpers.name: set_block
helpers.signature: fn native_set_block( &mut self, dimension: &str, pos: [i32; 3], state: BlockStateId, flags: i32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Sets a block in the current authoritative level through `Level.setBlock`. Returns false for another dimension, an invalid state, or no change. `flags` selects vanilla's neighbour and shape updates; Horizon sends every write to players whatever the flags. A block entity block gets its block entity. API 24.

helpers.name: neighbor_signal
helpers.signature: fn native_neighbor_signal(&mut self, dimension: &str, pos: [i32; 3]) -> i32
helpers.doc: The strongest redstone signal reaching the block at `pos` from its six neighbours, 0 to 15 (`SignalGetter.getBestNeighborSignal`, what a dispenser or a piston reads), in the level in place, `dimension`. 0 on a client's copy of the world and for another dimension. A mod's explosive, launcher or machine reads it in its block entity's tick to go off or switch on. API 96.

helpers.name: light
helpers.doc: The light at `pos` in the world in place, as `(block, sky)`, each 0 to 15 (`Level.getBrightness` for `LightLayer.BLOCK` and `LightLayer.SKY`). A solar panel checks for full sky light above it, a lamp or a mob farm for darkness. `(0, 0)` in a chunk that isn't loaded. Like the other reads here it reads the world this game holds: the level in place on a server, the server's copy on a client. API 97.

helpers.name: weather
helpers.doc: The rain and thunder levels of the world in place, each 0.0 to 1.0 (`Level.getRainLevel` and `Level.getThunderLevel`): what a solar panel or a wind turbine reads. Both 0 in the Nether and the End, which have no weather (`Level.canHaveWeather`). API 97.

helpers.name: day_time
helpers.doc: The world's time of day in ticks (`Level.getOverworldClockTime`), the same as `native_clock`'s `day_time`; it keeps counting past 24000, so take it modulo 24000 for the hour. API 97.

helpers.name: world_height
helpers.doc: The lowest block y and the height of the world in place (`LevelHeightAccessor.getMinY` and `getHeight`): how deep a quarry or a miner may dig. API 97.

helpers.name: max_stack_size
helpers.doc: The most of the item `item` one slot holds (`Item.getDefaultMaxStackSize`), or `None` for an unknown item: for a mod's container that fills or merges stacks itself. API 97.

helpers.name: item_model
helpers.signature: fn native_item_model( &self, batch: &mut HudBatch, item: &str, model: &str, at: [f32; 2], size: f32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Item `item`'s icon drawn with model `model` (`minecraft:paper` as `mymod:wheel_icon`, an `item_model` of a content mod's), as `native_item` draws one; false for an unknown item. API 111.

helpers.name: quad
helpers.signature: fn native_quad(&self, batch: &mut HudBatch, points: [[f32; 2]; 4], argb: u32)
helpers.doc: A quad of corners `points` (in order round it) in GUI pixels, `argb`: a wedge, a slanted bar, what `native_fill`'s rectangles can't draw. API 111.

helpers.name: mod_screen_open
helpers.doc: Opens a screen of mod `mod_id`'s own over the world: the screen hooks fire over it as over any other, so the mod draws it in `native_screen_render_post` and takes its clicks, scroll, keys and typing there; the mouse is freed, and Escape closes it. Every mod's own screen has the `NativeScreenView.id` `mod`, so a mod's screen hooks check `native_mod_screen()` is its own before drawing. It doesn't pause a single-player game (as the inventory doesn't). True when it is open: false while another screen is (or another mod's), over the title screen, a book, a sign editor, a dialog or a prompt, while the world loads, and anywhere but the window's own client (the server thread, a dedicated server). A gamepad can close it (B, Start) but not click on it: its clicks don't reach the mouse hooks. API 111.

helpers.name: mod_screen_close
helpers.doc: Closes mod `mod_id`'s own screen, if it is open. API 111.

helpers.name: mod_screen
helpers.doc: The mod whose own screen is open, if one is (Escape, or another screen replacing it, closes it). API 111.

helpers.name: clock
helpers.doc: The clock of the world this window shows, for client mods: its game time and time of day as the server last sent them (`ClientboundSetTimePacket`), advanced each tick between packets; none on the title screen. API 92.

helpers.name: block_state_property
helpers.signature: fn native_block_state_property( &self, state: BlockStateId, key: &str, ) -> Option<&str>
helpers.doc: Property `key` of block state `state` (a machine's `facing`, from the `state` `native_block_entity_submit` gets), if it has one: no lookup in the world, so cheap each frame. API 91.

helpers.name: set_item_entity
helpers.signature: fn native_set_item_entity( &mut self, dimension: &str, id: u32, stack: ItemStack, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Sets the stack of item entity `id` in the server level `dimension`, as a hopper's `addItem` leaves what it couldn't take (`ItemEntity.setItem`); an empty stack (count 0) removes the entity (`setItem(EMPTY)`, then `discard`). Players see it on their next tracker update. False when the level in place has no such item entity, or on a client. API 42.

helpers.name: update_output_neighbors
helpers.signature: fn native_update_output_neighbors( &mut self, dimension: &str, pos: [i32; 3], ) -> bool
helpers.doc: The block at `pos` changed its comparator output (`native_analog_output`) without changing its state: the comparators beside it, or behind a conductor there, read it again (`Level.updateNeighbourForOutputSignal`). Acts on the level in place: false (and nothing happens) when `dimension` is another, or this window isn't a server. API 64.

helpers.name: update_signal_neighbors
helpers.signature: fn native_update_signal_neighbors( &mut self, dimension: &str, pos: [i32; 3], ) -> bool
helpers.doc: The block at `pos` changed the signal it gives: its neighbours, and theirs (a block it powers passes the signal on), read it again, as around a lever (`Level.updateNeighborsAt`). Call it when the answer changes and once the block is placed. Acts on the level in place: false (and nothing happens) when `dimension` is another, or this window isn't a server. API 38.

helpers.name: block_entity_sync
helpers.doc: Sends clients the block at `pos` and its block entity's update tag (`native_block_entity_update_tag`) again, as `Level.sendBlockUpdated` does: with the level's other block changes, to the players who see its chunk, once however often it is called before then. Changes made in a block entity's tick go out at the start of the next tick, as vanilla's do (`ServerLevel.tick` broadcasts chunks before it ticks block entities). Call it when what clients show changed (a machine started), not for every tick's progress: a menu's data slots carry that. Nothing happens for an unloaded block. API 52.

helpers.name: play_local_sound
helpers.signature: fn native_play_local_sound( &mut self, sound: &str, at: [f64; 3], volume: f32, pitch: f32, delay: i32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Plays sound event `sound` (`minecraft:entity.generic.explode`, or a mod's own from its `assets/<id>/sounds.json`) at `at` for this player only, `delay` ticks from now (0 to 1200, a minute): a client mod's sound that waits, as thunder heard after the flash or a blast heard when its shock wave arrives. `volume` past 1 carries farther, as vanilla's attenuation does (16 blocks times the volume). False, with nothing played, on a server or for a value out of range; an event the resources don't have plays nothing, as vanilla's. API 83.

helpers.name: fill
helpers.signature: fn native_fill(&self, batch: &mut HudBatch, rect: [f32; 4], argb: u32)
helpers.doc: A rectangle in GUI pixels, `argb` (0x78000000 is the extras' box).

helpers.name: sprite
helpers.signature: fn native_sprite( &self, batch: &mut HudBatch, name: &str, src: [f32; 4], dst: [f32; 4], ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Part `src` (`[x, y, w, h]` in the sprite's own pixels) of sprite `name` (vanilla's `gui/...`, or a content mod's GUI texture `mymod:gui/...`), drawn stretched into `dst` (`[x, y, w, h]` in GUI pixels). False when there is no such sprite. API 19.

helpers.name: item
helpers.signature: fn native_item( &self, batch: &mut HudBatch, item: &str, at: [f32; 2], size: f32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Item `item`'s icon (`mymod:machine`) with its top left at `at`, `size` GUI pixels square (16 in a slot); false for an unknown item. API 20.

helpers.name: screen_title
helpers.doc: The open menu's title (the block's name, or the one it was given), as plain text. API 20.

helpers.name: data
helpers.doc: A data file of the game's resources, content mods' included (`data/mymod/machines.json`), when there is one: what a mod's content says, read at runtime. Only relative paths of plain names. API 20.

helpers.name: block
helpers.doc: The block at `pos` (`mymod:cable`; air where nothing is loaded). API 20.

helpers.name: block_property
helpers.doc: Property `key` of the block at `pos` (a machine's `facing`), if it has one. API 20.

helpers.name: insert_item
helpers.signature: fn native_insert_item( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], face: Direction, stack: ItemStack, ) -> Option<ItemStack>
helpers.doc: Puts `stack` into the container at `pos` (a chest, a furnace, a mod container) through its side `face`, as a hopper would, one by one, and returns what did not fit: a machine's auto-output. A composter takes one a call, and a client's copy of the world none. API 20.

helpers.name: cursor
helpers.doc: Where the mouse is, in GUI pixels. API 20.

helpers.name: text
helpers.signature: fn native_text( &self, batch: &mut HudBatch, text: &str, at: [f32; 2], rgb: u32, shadow: bool, )
helpers.doc: A line of text at `(x, y)` in GUI pixels, opaque `rgb`.

helpers.name: built_data
helpers.doc: The folder mod `mod_id`'s post-build step wrote into when the launcher built the game (`native-data/<id>/` in the build's version folder); None when the game's own path is unknown. API 41.

helpers.name: on
helpers.doc: Whether the player left mod `mod_id` on in Options > Mods. A mod turned off does nothing (check this first in each hook) until the launcher's next build leaves it out.

helpers.name: mod_key
helpers.signature: fn native_mod_key(&self, mod_id: &str, name: &str, default: &str) -> String
helpers.doc: The key the player chose for a mod's key `name`, else `default` (`key.keyboard.z`), as the WebAssembly mods' keys were kept (`key.<mod id>.<name>` in `horizon-mods.txt`).

helpers.name: setting
helpers.doc: A mod's setting `key` (one file per key in `native_data_dir`).

helpers.name: set_setting
helpers.doc: Keeps a mod's setting `key`.

helpers.name: set_block_property
helpers.signature: fn native_set_block_property( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], key: &str, value: &str, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Sets property `key` of the block at `pos` to `value`, as a furnace's tick sets its `lit` (`Level.setBlock` with `UPDATE_ALL`: neighbours and clients are told); true when the block changed, false when the block has no such property or value, or the property already has `value` (as `Level.setBlock` for an unchanged state). The block entity stays. API 18.

helpers.name: set_block_property_with
helpers.signature: fn native_set_block_property_with( &mut self, pos: [i32; 3], key: &str, value: &str, flags: i32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: `native_set_block_property` with `Level.setBlock`'s `flags`, as a brewing stand's tick sets its bottles with `flags::UPDATE_CLIENTS`. Players get the write whatever the flags (`flags`); false when this window isn't a server, and in each case `native_set_block_property` returns false. API 33.

helpers.name: config_dir
helpers.doc: The game's `config/` folder beside `options.txt`, shared by every mod as on Fabric and NeoForge: a mod names its own files in it (`config/<id>.json`, or a folder of its own). The same folder on the window, its server thread and a LAN host; a dedicated server's is in its own folder, beside `server.properties`. Made when missing. No `self`, so a mixin helper calls `Game::native_config_dir()` and a trait mod `Host::config_dir`. API 26.

helpers.name: panel_items
helpers.signature: fn native_panel_items(&mut self, mod_id: &str, items: Vec<NativeStack>)
helpers.doc: Shows the panel beside container screens with these items (at most 8192), as the game's own slots in pages, with a search box; the player's clicks, searches and keys over items come back as `native_panel_event`. The panel is the last mod's to show one; empty items and no recipe page take yours away, except that an empty reply to a non-empty Search keeps its field editable. A clear outside that event still removes the panel (as when a viewer closes).

helpers.name: recipes_of_type
helpers.doc: The recipes of type `kind` (`mymod:crusher`), a type outside `minecraft`, from `data/<namespace>/recipe/*.json` of the content mods (`.hmod`) and the world's data packs, in file order: each one's id and its file as JSON, for the mod to read as it likes. A data pack changes them on `/reload`, so look them up again when you need them. Empty for a type nobody uses and outside a world. These are the server's table on the server thread, a dedicated server or a LAN host; a client, the single-player window included, sees only the content mods' recipes, not the world's data packs', unless a mod had the server send it the type (`native_datapack_sync`). API 36.

helpers.name: recipe_ingredient
helpers.doc: An ingredient as a recipe's JSON names it: an item, a `#tag`, or a list of them, a bare id as `minecraft:` (as vanilla reads it); `test` says whether a stack fits. Items the game doesn't know are left out; None when nothing is left (an unknown or empty tag, for one) and outside a world. API 36.

helpers.name: recipe_result
helpers.doc: A stack as a recipe's `result` names it: `id` (a bare one as `minecraft:`), `count` (1 by default, up to 99) and `components`. None without an `id`, for an item the game doesn't know or a count outside that, and outside a world. API 36.

helpers.name: known_recipes
helpers.doc: The `book_id`s of the recipes the player's recipe book holds now (the server's book on a server); empty outside a world.

helpers.name: place_recipe
helpers.signature: fn native_place_recipe(&mut self, book_id: i32, all: bool) -> Result<(), String>
helpers.doc: Places a recipe in the open screen's grid as a click in the recipe book does (`ServerboundPlaceRecipePacket`): the inventory's grid, a crafting table's or a mod menu type's crafting grid. `all` places as many as the items allow, as with Shift. Refused while no such screen is open and for a recipe the player's book doesn't hold; one missing items shows as a ghost.

helpers.name: give
helpers.signature: fn native_give(&mut self, item: &str, count: u32) -> Result<(), String>
helpers.doc: Creative mode only: gives the player `count` of `item` (`minecraft:diamond`) as taking it from the creative inventory does (`ServerboundSetCreativeModeSlot`): the selected slot first, then the hotbar, then the inventory. The count is cut to one stack.

helpers.name: push_player
helpers.doc: For a client mod: a push added to the local player's velocity, in blocks a tick, as an explosion's knockback is (the window's player moves itself, as vanilla's client does). Each component is clamped to -4..4; a spectator, or a value that is not a number, is left alone. API 105.

helpers.name: set_flying_speed
helpers.signature: fn native_set_flying_speed(&mut self, player: u128, speed: Option<f32>) -> bool
helpers.doc: For a server mod: `player`'s creative flying speed (vanilla's 0.05 when none, at most `FLYING_MAX`), kept on the server's player and sent to their client. A respawn or a game mode change keeps it, and it is saved with the player (`abilities.flySpeed`, as vanilla saves it). False for a player not here or a client of a server, and inside a player's hook, where the server's player list is busy: call it from a tick hook. API 105.

helpers.name: item_stack
helpers.signature: fn native_item_stack( &self, batch: &mut HudBatch, stack: &ItemStack, at: [f32; 2], size: f32, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Draw a stack and its slot decorations, except the count, at `at`, `size` GUI pixels square. False when nothing was drawn: an unknown item or an empty stack (air, or a count of 0, as `ItemStack.isEmpty`). API 313.

helpers.name: mod_image
helpers.signature: fn native_mod_image(&mut self, width: u32, height: u32, rgba: &[u8]) -> bool
helpers.doc: A mod's own RGBA image, uploaded into the HUD atlas slot [`MOD_IMAGE_SPRITE`](crate::hud::MOD_IMAGE_SPRITE) and drawn with `native_sprite`: its own source rectangle crops and stretches it. `rgba` is `width * height` pixels of four bytes, each side at most [`MOD_IMAGE_SIZE`](crate::hud::MOD_IMAGE_SIZE); false when it is not that size. The upload costs a texture patch of the image, so send one when the image changed, not every frame. API 355.

helpers.name: instance_dir
helpers.doc: The instance (game) folder, which its players share: `saves/`, `resourcepacks/`, `shaderpacks/` and `horizon-mods/` are in it, and the title's screens create worlds and read packs there. A world's own `datapacks/` is in that world's folder (`saves/<world>/datapacks`). The folder the game runs in (`--player-dir` moves a player's options and servers only, not the instance). Nothing is created. API 326.

helpers.name: camera
helpers.doc: The most recently extracted world frame's camera, if one exists. During GUI rendering this is the current frame, including bob/spin and FOV.

helpers.name: block_collision
helpers.doc: Collision boxes in block-local coordinates with an empty collision context.

helpers.name: entity
helpers.doc: The entity `id` (the id events carry) as a handle for the `entity_*` methods: None with no world open, or for no such entity in the level in place or among the server's players. On a client (API @API:client_entity_refs@), any entity the server shows this window, this window's own player included. API 373.

helpers.name: level
helpers.doc: The level `dimension` (`minecraft:the_nether`) as a handle: None on a client, with no world open, or for a dimension the server hasn't loaded. API 373.

helpers.name: entity_position
helpers.doc: The entity's position (`Entity.position`): its feet, the middle of its box for a painting or an item frame. On a client, where the window shows it (another entity eases toward the server's moves); an entity tracked without a list of its own is where the server last put it. API 373.

helpers.name: entity_block_position
helpers.doc: The block the entity's position is in (`Entity.blockPosition`). API 373.

helpers.name: entity_rotation
helpers.doc: The entity's yaw and pitch in degrees (`Entity.getYRot`, `getXRot`); 0 for the kinds that don't turn. API 373.

helpers.name: entity_kind
helpers.doc: The entity's type (`Entity.getType`): `minecraft:zombie`. API 373.

helpers.name: entity_uuid
helpers.signature: fn native_entity_uuid(&mut self, entity: EntityRef) -> Option<u128>
helpers.doc: The entity's UUID (`Entity.getUUID`), the one it is saved with; an entity that has none yet gets it now, as a new vanilla entity does. On a client, the one the server added it with (a player's is its profile's). API 373.

helpers.name: entity_level
helpers.doc: The level the entity is in (`Entity.level`): on a client, the client's level. API 373.

helpers.name: recipe_book_category
helpers.doc: The validated category and icon of a custom recipe type, or None for an undeclared/invalid type, before resources load, or outside a world. Rebuilt when the recipe table changes. Does not unlock any recipes.

helpers.name: screen_pos
helpers.doc: The block of the mod screen that is open (`native_screen`), as the server named it when the block opened its menu type; None when no mod screen is open. 401.

helpers.name: screen_extra_data
helpers.doc: What the block's mod wrote for the mod screen that is open (`native_menu_extra_data` on the server), empty when it wrote nothing; None when no mod screen is open. 401.

helpers.name: client_state
helpers.doc: Client/window/connection state, including when menus cover the world.

helpers.name: client_entities
helpers.doc: Bulk client render data. Unlike EntityRef, this snapshot expires independently of handles.

helpers.name: client_heads
helpers.signature: fn native_client_heads(&self, ids: &[u32], partial: f64) -> Vec<NativeClientHead>
helpers.doc: Requested model heads at a finite partial tick in 0..=1; at most 4096 IDs. Name bounds are vanilla's, without dispatching name hooks recursively.

helpers.name: client_profiles
helpers.doc: Player-list profiles with skin/cosmetic resolution through the client's normal cache.

helpers.name: client_visual_clear
helpers.doc: Whether a finite segment of at most 1024 blocks meets no visual block shape. Glass is transparent; partial blocks use their visual shapes. Unloaded paths refuse.

helpers.name: client_block_obstruction
helpers.doc: Loaded block's full-collision and render-occlusion facts, in that order.

helpers.name: gui_paint
helpers.doc: Paint GUI extraction calls through this window's atlas, including player faces.

helpers.name: gui_nine_slice
helpers.signature: fn native_gui_nine_slice( &self, batch: &mut HudBatch, sprite: &str, rect: [f32; 4], color: u32, )
helpers.doc: Vanilla's nine-slice widget rendering. `color` is ARGB, as `fill` uses.

helpers.name: gui_tooltip
helpers.signature: fn native_gui_tooltip(&self, batch: &mut HudBatch, lines: &[Text], at: [f32; 2])
helpers.doc: A vanilla tooltip at the cursor, in GUI pixels.

helpers.name: set_mod_key
helpers.signature: fn native_set_mod_key( &mut self, mod_id: &str, name: &str, key: Option<&str>, ) -> bool
helpers.doc: Save a mod binding, or restore its default with None. No write when unchanged.

helpers.name: client_action_bar
helpers.signature: fn native_client_action_bar(&mut self, text: Text, animate: bool)
helpers.doc: Set this client's action bar, with the normal timer; no server command or packet.

helpers.name: text_width
helpers.doc: The width of `text` in GUI pixels.

helpers.name: playing
helpers.doc: Playing, with nothing over the world: keys and zoom apply.

helpers.name: window
helpers.doc: This `Game` is the window's, not a server's.

helpers.name: player
helpers.doc: The player, in a world.

goals.name: Float
goals.doc: FloatGoal: jump (swim up) while deeper than the jump threshold or in lava.

goals.name: ClimbOnTopOfPowderSnow
goals.doc: `ClimbOnTopOfPowderSnowGoal`: a powder-snow walker standing in powder snow jumps while the block above is powder snow or has no collision.

goals.name: Panic
goals.doc: PanicGoal: flee to a random position after panic-causing damage (or towards water while burning).

goals.name: HurtByTarget
goals.doc: HurtByTargetGoal (optionally alerting others of the same species).

goals.name: AvoidEntity
constructors: AvoidEntity::new(what: Avoid, max_dist: f32, walk: f64, sprint: f64)

goals.name: Breed
goals.doc: BreedGoal: walk to a partner in love and breed after 60 ticks.

goals.name: FollowMob
goals.doc: `FollowMobGoal` `(mob, speed, stopDistance, areaSize)`: follows the first visible mob of another class within `area` blocks and keeps `stop` away from it (a parrot hovers by the other animals).  Left out: vanilla also backs away when the followed mob's look control wants this mob's position; only another `FollowMobGoal` mob of a different class would look at it, and parrots are the only ones that have the goal.
constructors: FollowMob::new(speed: f64, stop: f32, area: f32)

goals.name: RestrictSun
goals.doc: RestrictSunGoal: avoid sunlit nodes while it is bright outside.

goals.name: EatBlock
goals.doc: EatBlockGoal (sheep): eat short grass or turn grass blocks to dirt.

goals.name: BreathAir
goals.doc: BreathAirGoal: swim up to air when the air supply runs low.

goals.name: TryFindWater
goals.doc: TryFindLiquidGoal (water): head for nearby water when stranded on land.

docs.name: Native mods
docs.text:
`native_explosion_entities(dimension, center, entities)` (server) runs after `native_explosion_detonate`, before an explosion at `center` hurts and pushes anything: `entities` holds the ids of the entities in its reach (`ServerExplosion.hurtEntities`), players aside, which `native_living_incoming_damage` hears. Take out the ids to spare: they are neither hurt nor pushed, as NeoForge's `ExplosionEvent.Detonate` does with its entity list. Bundles need "hooks": @API:explosion_entities@.

`native_chat_suggestion_applied(original, start, end, suggestion, input)` reports a suggestion accepted in the open chat by Tab or a mouse click, after the text and caret have changed. `original` is the suggestion list's input before any completion; `start` and `end` are the replaced range in that string, in Java UTF-16 units (end exclusive). They keep referring to `original` when Tab cycles through the list. `suggestion` is the selected replacement text, and `input` is the actual resulting field value, including any length-limit truncation. This is a read-only notification: previews, list navigation, server replies, ordinary typing and command-block editors do not fire it. Trait mods implement `Hooks::chat_suggestion_applied`; mixin bundles use `chat_suggestion_applied`, hook version 1. Bundles need "hooks": @API:chat_suggestion_applied@ (assigned at merge).

API 362 adds `native_compute_fov_modifier(player, base, modifier)` on the client each tick for the local player's FOV scale, after vanilla effects and before zoom and camera easing. `player` contains the calculation inputs and `base` is the original scale. Non-finite modifiers or values outside 0.01..=10 fall back to `base`. It does not affect a spectator camera on a mob. Bundles need "hooks": 362.

The client hook `native_client_packet(packet)` hears each play packet the server sends, decoded (`ClientboundPlayPacket`, `horizon_protocol`'s `play::Clientbound`), just before the game handles it, custom payloads included and in the order they came. It only reads: the game handles the packet as it would without the mod. Packets the network thread handles itself (keep-alives, bundle delimiters, resource packs, cookies, server links, transfers, disconnects, the configuration switch, `minecraft:brand`, far terrain tiles) and the configuration phase are not heard. Bundles need "hooks": 408.
